articles.title: Week 11 College Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups: Legend Glasker, Elijah Lofton among top adds
articles.summary: Eric Froton takes you through his top adds off the college fantasy football waiver wire for Week 11.
articles.body:
Hard to believe we're already on the cusp of the playoffs, as the College Fantasy Football regular season is a sprint, not a marathon. With the massive Week 9 and 10 byes now out of the way, here are my top Week 11 waiver wire pickups.

Thomas Castellanos, Texas Tech (36% rostered on Yahoo)

Castellanos had been used mostly in gadget packages before last week's victory over Arizona when he beat the Wildcats 34-26 with 117 rushing yards and 31.5 points in his first start of the year. On Saturday, Castellanos had the pleasure of facing West Virginia's 121st-ranked defense and promptly led all P4 signal callers with 44.68 points thanks to his five touchdown passes, 362 passing yards and 102 rushing yards. His 63.3% rushing success rate and 0.28 EPA/play average shows the explosive traits Castellanos possesses, and he should post a third-consecutive 30+ point game against Oklahoma State's porous secondary that ranks 131st in completions of 20+ yards allowed (22.1%).

Marshall missed Kansas' last game at TCU, but recorded 20+ points in each of his previous four appearances heading into Saturday's contest versus UCF. He didn't disappoint, rushing for 125 yards and two rushing touchdowns for 34.9 points, which was the fifth-highest quarterback score of Week 10. Marshall ranks fifth among all P4 quarterbacks in rushing yards and is definitely startable next weekend against CFF dream opponent West Virginia.

The Georgia Southern transfer has been a major boost for the UC offense, scoring at least 23 points in six games while clearing the 25-point mark in three of his past four despite facing Big 12 powerhouses Houston, Utah and Texas Tech the past three weeks. He should have another excellent game this weekend against Iowa State's struggling secondary that ranks 130th with 7.5 yards per dropback allowed.

Bo MacCormack III, Boston College (4% rostered)

MacCormack has taken over the starting gig with Evan Dickey out for the season, and done so emphatically with two 100-yard performances under his belt in just three games as a starter. He accounted for 71% of the Eagles' rushing production against FSU on Saturday, and was the primary offensive weapon on a day when BC managed just 320 total yards in the 31-24 defeat. A grinder whose father is a former Golden Gloves champion, MacCormack will have tough sledding this week against Notre Dame, but will be a wheels-up starter in Week 12 versus Syracuse.

Phillips racked up 1,921 yards, 6.5 YPC and 19 touchdowns for South Dakota last year, and generated significant buzz in fall camp, suggesting he might be able to challenge incumbent starter Kamari Moulton for carries this year. While he served as a rotational member of Iowa's backfield for most of the year, opportunity knocked when Kamari Moulton suffered a season-ending injury a few weeks ago. Phillips worked behind Xavier Williams last week in a 30-0 drubbing of Wisconsin, but outcarried the rest of the Hawkeyes' backfield 21-to-5 with 128 yards and 15.2 points in the 24-10 victory over Northwestern. Phillips looked dynamic producing 4.5 yards after contact on the day despite not finding the end zone. He has a prime-time matchup this weekend against Purdue's dismal 103rd-ranked defense that is allowing 5.6 YPC (127th in FBS).

Amari Thomas, Florida State (0% rostered)

Thomas had received only four carries prior to this week, but when star RB Ousmane Kromah went down for the year with an injury and Tre Wisner was questionable to play all week, FSU plugged in Thomas to the starting role. He erupted for 19 carries, 98 yards and two touchdowns in the 31-24 victory over BC, cementing himself as a valuable contributor against Pitt and NC State the next two weeks.

Nolan James Jr., Notre Dame (47% rostered)

James has scored 10+ points in every single game this season, and has averaged 17.6 PPG over his past five contests where he has been the lead back. He is officially the Irish's lead RB and is an auto-start against Boston College this weekend, grab him if available.

One of the most dangerous freshmen in the country, Glasker has proven to be the most important aerial weapon for a Cougars offense that averages 31 PPG, 5.2 points per scoring opportunity (19th) and is a College Football Playoff contender. Glasker leads the P4 with five receptions of 50+ yards and is producing an impressive 13.9 yards per target and 18.3 yards per reception. The Big 12 has been top-to-bottom the most impactful P4 conference from a CFF perspective, and BYU has arguably the most favorable closing stretch of any Power Conference team facing Baylor, at Kansas and Cincinnati over the final three weeks. With Glasker accounting for at least 10+ points with 4+ receptions and 54+ yards in each of his last five games, he is an auto-start in the playoffs and is only rostered in 1/5th of all Yahoo leagues.

Giovanni Richardson, Arizona (1% rostered)

Richardson has been electric every time he's stepped on the field healthy this season, averaging 14.3 PPG in the four contests where he was able to play most of the game. He has reached 90+ yards three times despite barely suiting up from Sept. 12- Oct. 31 due to injury. Richardson has been back for two games and has been a revelation, catching 17-of-21 passes for 264 yards and 33.5 points despite not reaching the end zone yet in 2026. He has all the traits of a shifty separator from the slot who wins off the line and on the break. He will be heavily targeted against Big 12 favorite Utah this weekend, and should be startable against Kansas State and Arizona State to finish out the regular season.

Every time I've watched UCF since October, Derry has jumped off the screen. The unquestioned Golden Knights WR1, Derry has been a demon over the past five games catching 35-of-50 targets for 460 yards and four touchdowns. He's an excellent streamer versus Arizona State this weekend after catching eight passes for 143 yards and a touchdown in a 33-32 win over Kansas on Saturday.

Mazeo Bennett Jr., South Carolina (2% rostered)

It baffles me how Bennett has scored 13+ points in each of his past five games, and wrested the WR1 role away from one-dimensional Nyck Harbor, yet he's still only rostered in 2% of leagues? QB LaNorris Sellers emerged over the past month and has taken Bennett along for the ride. He's a superb starting option against SEC doormat Arkansas this weekend.

Miami clearly needed to reestablish its offensive identity after losing superstar WR Malachi Toney for the remainder of the regular season. It was Duke transfer Cooper Barkate and Lofton who QB Darian Mensah leaned on when he needed a completion, pegging Lofton with 13 targets for seven receptions, 113 yards and a touchdown for a season-high 20.8 points against the vaunted ND defense. He has secured multiple receptions in each of his past seven games with three touchdowns in that span, and is trending up after just posting his two best receiving performances of the year. Lofton will continue to be a focal point of the Miami passing attack against Duke, Virginia Tech and BC the last three weeks of the season.

There are relatively few tight ends who have the ability to produce double-digit point totals on a given week. Livingston was sparsely used in September, but has come of age with 12 receptions for 150 yards and four touchdowns over his past five games, including five receptions for 74 yards and three touchdowns in the past two games. He's a suitable dice roll if you need more production from your tight end.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Booms and Busts: Mega-star WRs show out in otherwise wonky Week 9
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski examines Week 9's winners and losers from Sunday's action.
articles.body:
In the middle of a wonky Week 9, I looked to the wide receiver board for comfort. Maybe some alpha wideouts posting big numbers would soothe the nerves a little bit. Alas, even that roundup brought some agita. The NFL is a whirlwind, now and forever.

The Week 9 receivers on the outside are names you know by heart. CeeDee Lamb (10-195-1) went bananas with George Pickens unavailable. Puka Nacua (14-150-1) was unstoppable against Washington, the one reliable downfield option Matthew Stafford has. Ja'Marr Chase (10-155-1) was worth the early alarm, torching the Falcons in Spain. And as I compose this weekly notebook, the newly-minted stars of the Packers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, are crushing against the New England secondary.

But the breaking Nacua news overshadows the day. Nacua was hurt on his final snap against the Commanders — on a running play of all things — and needs an MRI on his knee Monday. The Rams don't believe Nacua has a torn ACL, but any MRI is a scary prospect. Nacua's production over the last six games has been too good to be true: 84 targets, 65 catches, 641 yards, five total touchdowns.

The funny thing about the Rams, even with Nacua going nuclear, the L.A. offense hasn't been special. It's scored a modest 44 points in the last two weeks, despite playing the Chargers and Commanders. There was the 18-16 loss to Arizona in Week 6. Forget the Rams as preseason favorites; they're no guarantee to be a playoff team. And if Nacua misses time, all bets are clearly off.

Lamb is doing the target thing for the Cowboys, too. He had 16 looks in the win at Indianapolis, what we want from our first-rounders. That makes 83 targets in six games for Lamb, and while the Pickens' absence made it easier for Prescott to look Lamb's way, the Cowboys will always lean that way. San Francisco is a challenge next week, then come favorable draws against Tennessee and Philadelphia.

I was hopeful Ryan Flournoy would spread his wings without Pickens, but that narrative died on the vine. Flournoy had a late 46-yard catch to partially save his day, but a 2-53-0 log on three targets goes down as a loss. It just underscores the variance at the receiver position — Flournoy had four productive weeks as the team's No. 3 receiver, then was mostly invisible here.

Joe Burrow and the Bengals are usually a palate-cleaning offense, and Week 9 applies. The Bengals romped over Atlanta 34-17 in the morning game, with Burrow throwing for three scores and running in another. Burrow steered most of the work to Chase (12 targets), though Tee Higgins salvaged a 5-32-2 day on his six opportunities. Ah, touchdown deodorant. Chase Brown continues to be a net loss for fantasy managers, getting just 12 chances and making a credible 75 yards. The efficiency is good, the workload was not. He also didn't score a touchdown. Samaje Perine (11-43-0) is playing more than anyone imagined.

The Texans continue to play against type, a pass-first offense with a stagnant running game and a defense that's far less than expected. C.J. Stroud continued his redemption song, throwing for five touchdowns and 384 yards against the sorry Chargers. The Houston passing tree continues to be wide, as Kayshon Boutte (4-125-2) and Tank Dell (4-105-1) had the most productive days, and Nico Collins was targeted just four times (4-55-1). Before the year, we thought this would be a small pie with Collins getting the biggest piece; it's turned into a larger pie, but the shares are split rather evenly. The Browns are next up.

Familiar names pushed back to the top of the running back board, with Kenneth Walker III, Bijan Robinson and Christian McCaffrey all scoring well. Walker had three total touchdowns, two in the receiving game, and the Falcons finally got Robinson going again in their passing game (47 yards). McCaffrey continues to be ordinary in efficiency, but a couple of scores got him home in a lopsided win over the Raiders. Widely available Jordan Watkins (4-86-1) was the best of the San Francisco receivers.

I was hopeful that Alvin Kamara could get a bigger role with Kendre Miller cut, but the Saints dialed up Audric Estime (15-72-1) as the primary back against the Browns. Maybe it's not a surprise that Estime was used, but I didn't expect him to be this effective. Chris Olave (7-98-0) was the target hog for the Saints, though rookie Jordyn Tyson (4-30-0) had five targets and lost a touchdown at the one-yard line. The Saints still haven't scored a first-half touchdown all year, but Tyler Shough usually has credible fantasy stats when the day is over.

Detroit games are usually a blast on both sides of the ball, but just 498 yards of offense hit the field between the Lions and Dolphins. Jared Goff was limited to 170 yards and no touchdowns — although the Miami defense isn't great, it's not a punching bag, either. Jahmyr Gibbs had a 20-74-1 rushing log but no receptions. Malik Willis was one of my favorite Week 9 sleepers, but this one stayed asleep — no touchdowns, just 135 total yards. Perhaps the groin injury he dealt with this week was more of a problem on Sunday than anticipated.

Usually, solving for volume will get you fantasy glory, but Devin Singletary did very little with 23 touches (just 39 total yards). The lone New York touchdown was a Jameis Winston pass to Isaiah Likely — Winston briefly replaced an injured J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy didn't have his best showing, posting a 6.7 YPA and taking five sacks. The Eagles offense stayed shipwrecked, though a 22-yard Saquon Barkley day was at least helped by a short touchdown run. There are too many dead offenses in fantasy; the Eagles are perilously close to becoming one.

The Jets at times have been a fun fantasy offense, but it's not always easy to read the pregame signals. Last week it was Omar Cooper Jr. toasting a bagel while Adonai Mitchell went off — at Kansas City, Cooper spread his wings (8-58-0) in a PPR scam, but Mitchell went catchless on seven targets. We expected better with Garrett Wilson out. Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both made 4.1 YPC with their work, though Hall had 15 rushes to Allen's eight. The Jets perhaps were showcasing Hall, someone who should draw interest as we close in on Tuesday's trading deadline.

articles.title: Anuj Shrivatri becomes India’s 100th chess Grandmaster
articles.summary: PUNE: Anuj Shrivatri has become India's 100th chess grandmaster and the first from Madhya Pradesh after winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess
articles.body: PUNE: Anuj Shrivatri has become India's 100th chess grandmaster and the first from Madhya Pradesh after winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship Governor Henry S. Oaminal Cup in the Philippines on Sunday.The 22-year-old from Katni, ranked India No. 76, secured the title through a special format that awarded a direct GM title to the winner, bypassing the usual requirement of three norms across 27 games and an Elo rating of 2500. His peak rating was 2483, achieved in June.Fourth seed Anuj, rated 2450, lost to home player Arca Karlo in the opening round but recovered strongly, winning six of his next eight games to finish with seven points. He finished half a point ahead of Vietnam GM Nguyen Duc Hoa and pocketed $3,000. The format meant Anuj faced only two players from the top 10 seeds and none rated higher than him. He finished with a performance rating of 2586, short of the 2600 required for a conventional GM norm, and is expected to gain around 15 rating points.Several Indian players, including Ayush Sharma, Neelash Saha, Nitish Belurkar, Mohd Imran and Ajay Parvathareddy, appeared better placed to become the country’s 100th GM, having already met either the norm or rating requirement. However, Anuj seized the opportunity to enter the record books.An International Master since 2019, Anuj becomes the latest Indian to earn the GM title through a special Fide-approved event. Divya Deshmukh, too, became India's fourth female GM through the Women's World Cup rather than the conventional route.India is not the first country to reach 100 grandmasters. Russia, the US, Ukraine and Germany have already crossed the milestone, with Russia boasting more than 250. More than 2,000 players have been awarded the GM title worldwide.The ASEAN Plus tournament was eligible to award a direct GM title provided at least four GMs and six IMs competed in every round. Although India is not part of the 11-member ASEAN chess bloc, Indian players were allowed to participate.First GM: V Anand, in 1988100th GM: Anuj ShrivatriRecent surge: 80 of India’s 100 GMs have emerged since 2010Last 6-7 years: 35 players have earned the titleState leaders: Tamil Nadu has nearly 40 GMs, while Maharashtra has over 10Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: As Magnus Carlsen and 23 others await, Total Chess chief defends fast classical-only group stage: ‘Good way to do it’ | Exclusive
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: World No.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen and 23 other players are set to take over the board at the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot in Budapest, but the build-up to the event has been shadowed by questions about its format.Speaking exclusively to TimesofIndia.com, Total Chess World Championship chief Kjell Madland defended the pilot’s format, under which qualification for the semi-finals is decided purely by fast classical. Rapid and Blitz come into play only after the group stage, which means 20 of the 24 players will not play either format before they are out of the race for the title.The tournament begins on November 10 at the Anantara New York Palace in Budapest, Hungary. A nine-round Swiss-system blitz tournament and the opening ceremony are held on the same day.Next up, the 24 players are then split into four groups of six, with the four highest-rated players in separate groups. Each group plays a double round robin at fast classical, which gives 45 minutes per player and a 30-second increment from move one, with three points for a win and one for a draw.The four group winners go through to the semi-finals, where they play Rapid and Blitz as well as fast classical. The other 20 players will play for positions 5 to 24 in all three formats, but they will not be in the race for the finale, which will take place on November 20.Madland, the founder and CEO of Norway Chess and the Total Chess World Championship Tour, rejected the suggestion that those 20 players are sidelined.“They are not eliminated,” he told this website. “All the players will play all the games until the last day.”The nine-round Blitz Swiss does not count towards qualification, but its standings break ties in the group tables. “If players are tied in the group stage, then we will look at the results in the blitz tournament to decide who is number two, three and four,” Madland added.He said the group stage uses fast classical because the time control, announced by FIDE in September 2025, is relatively new, and this is the best way to test it.“Since fast classical is a new format, it’s also good to have attention on this, so we think this is a good way to do it,” he said. “After that, the number one in all the groups will fight for first place, the number two will fight for the next place, and so on. But all the players will play all the games.”The knockouts use a different structure. The semi-finals, the third-place match and the final are each played over two days. Every day has four Blitz games, then two Rapid games, then one fast classical game, and scores reset each day. If the two days are split or both level, an Armageddon game decides the match. White gets ten minutes with no increment, and Black gets seven minutes with a one-second increment from move 41. A draw, in this case, wins the match for Black.Madland accepted that the format will draw questions. “Of course, we need to find a good way to do it. This is what we have done, and the players like it,” he noted. “Hopefully it will be good, but there will always be some questions about this and that. Hopefully this will work well.”He said the pilot status leaves room to adjust, though not drastically.“We don’t think we will do big adjustments. Hopefully we don’t need to think about that,” he said. “But when we have the pilot, it’s of course much easier if something is needed with rules and regulations. That’s possible. This is of course the reason we have this pilot, to test everything.”The pilot is the opening event of the Total Chess World Championship Tour 2026–27, which offers two places in the 2028 Candidates Tournament. It was announced by Norway Chess in October 2025, is endorsed by FIDE, and is co-organised with the Hungarian Chess Federation.Madland said the response so far has been positive.“We have received a lot of good feedback from everywhere, from players, from media and from fans,” he said. “People are very open to this, and I feel that people have also waited for something like this, because combining all the formats is a way to find the best players.”On why the format was built this way, he said: “I had a feeling for some years that we should build something that included everything, because we have talked with players, fans, media and everything.” He added that it would help the sport grow “in the media, in OTT and TV channels, in media deals.”“I hope people find this very interesting, and also that they are open to seeing that chess needs to change a bit to meet the new audience, so there will be more interest in it,” he said.The 24 participants of the Total Chess articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 9 RB Report: Breece Hall returns for Jets, sends Braelon Allen back to secondary role
articles.summary: Breece Hall was back in the fold for the Jets, plus more takeaways from key backfield splits for fantasy football in Week 9.
articles.body:
Welcome back for another edition of the fantasy football running back report. In Week 9, we have a few important backfields to highlight and break down for fantasy on a pretty lackluster Sunday afternoon overall for fantasy scoring, particularly at the RB position. While the fantasy points weren't flowing, there's still enough that we can gather to help inform us in our lineup decisions moving forward.

Let's dive in on some committee backfields and what to make of them as we approach Week 10.

Hall was back after missing the past five games due to a quad injury. In his stead, Allen had filled in admirably, putting up top-10 RB fantasy numbers from Weeks 4-8. Over that stretch, Allen averaged 15.2 fantasy points per game in half-PPR formats. He had four straight games with double-digit fantasy points going into Week 9. If you were fortunate enough to snag Allen, you were living a fantasy manager's dream.

But things came crashing down to earth in Week 9 against the Chiefs. We expected Hall to retain his lead-back role with Allen mixing in, keeping a role in the offense, albeit lesser than when Hall was out. But it wasn't exactly the 50-50 split we thought it would be, as Hall out-touched Allen, 18-10. Neither back went wild for managers given the tough road matchup against Kansas City. That will play a big factor in how we evaluate this backfield.

I'm willing to chalk this up to being a poor game script and situation for both backs. The Jets offense struggled to move the ball and it was probably a gift Hall and Allen got to those fantasy totals. New York also wanted to work Hall back up to speed while keeping Allen involved. WR Garrett Wilson (concussion) being out also doesn't help the unit overall.

So if we look ahead to Week 10 against the Bills, it should be easier for the Jets to move the ball. If Wilson is back, that could take some opportunities away in the passing game from each back. If Hall maintains this volume, he'll be a low-end RB2/3. Allen is more of a flex play at this point but is worth keeping on your roster in case something happens to Hall again.

We may have to graduate the Broncos' backfield out of this series now that Coleman has taken things over. But we do have to see how the splits go once RB RJ Harvey is off injured reserve. Until then, it appears to be Coleman's job and Dobbins continues to fall further out of favor with head coach Sean Payton.

Coleman wasn't very efficient with his touches, but it was clear we were going to get a response from the Panthers' defense after DC Ejiro Evero was fired following the loss last week on TNF to the Packers. So with Todd Wash taking over the defense, there was an emphasis on stopping the run given what we've seen from Denver's passing game.

Even so, Coleman was able to get home and is trending toward an RB1 finish with 16.8 fantasy points. He commanded most of the RB touches and scored a key TD in the red zone in the second half. The Broncos head into the bye in Week 10, so Coleman will be out of service. They'll face the Raiders in Week 11, Coleman will be a very strong RB2 play in that contest. Denver also has a great schedule down the stretch and one could assume Coleman, as a rookie, will only get better with more reps.

We just need to hope that the eventual return of Harvey doesn't cut into Coleman's workload too much. There's a chance Harvey retains the passing-down role while Coleman handles most of the ground work and goal-line carries. That would still make him very valuable for fantasy but limit his ceiling a bit.

As the NFL Trade Deadline looms on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET, it appears the Colts are going to hold onto Taylor. But the way the offense has been deploying the running backs the past few weeks, it's looking like this could be more of a committee the rest of 2026. The Colts could make a few more moves before the deadline to position themselves for additional draft picks. With the playoffs not on the menu this season, Indy wants to get a look at McGowan, who scored his first NFL touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys.

Taylor still got most of the work but failed to get to double-digit fantasy points for a second straight week. JT was also had some bad luck. He was taken out of the game on 3rd-and-goal because he lost his shoe , which allowed McGowan to score.

This is a tough situation. In a perfect world, Taylor gets traded to a contender and is in a much better environment for fantasy. With Indianapolis not playing for anything, it's unlikely Taylor gets his usual touch volume moving forward as McGowan could continue to see more looks.

I think JT will have some games where the Colts let him run wild and he gets home for fantasy managers. But the organization also doesn't care about your fantasy team. Taylor is less of an RB1 and more of an RB2 with upside who could continue to trend in the wrong direction. It may be tough to start him later in the season once the fantasy playoffs roll around, too.

McGowan is looking like a fringe flex option, but a player who could slowly see his role increase if he continues to be efficient with his runs. T he rookie isn't a bad stash off the waiver wire going into Week 10 , depending on what happens at the deadline on Tuesday.

The Seahawks got Charb back in the lineup last week, the first time he was on the field since tearing his ACL last season. He was eased back into action with just nine touches while playing 23 snaps (37%). George Holani saw 11 snaps last week as well, while rookie Jadarian Price played the most with 48%. But we saw a clear shift in Week 9.

Charbonnet got the bulk of the ground work while Price was the receiving back. The AJ Barner goal-line TD is frustrating, but other than that, this is an encouraging sign for managers of both backs, really. The Seahawks didn't need much to get past the lowly Cardinals and let the defense carry them.

For Charbonnet, this script is good news. Sam Darnold was out and the passing game took a bit of a hit with Drew Lock under center. That's concerning in that it could mean Seattle's drives stall out more often against tougher opponents. It would hurt Price's stock since we'd see Jaxon Smith-Njigba much more involved than Sunday (7-51 on 10 targets).

If you have Charb, he's looking like he could pay off late in the season after being a stash for the first half. Even if he isn't particularly explosive, he'll eat up carries and should see goal-line touches. Charbonnet is working his way into the RB2 convo but is more of an RB3/flex play at the moment. Price is more volatile but could provide decent flex value in PPR formats and would need to step up if anything happens to Charb.

articles.summary: Northern Arizona Lumberjacks (0-2) at Arizona Wildcats (1-1)Tucson, Arizona; Tuesday, 9 p. 5 Arizona hosts Northern Arizona after Motiejus Krivas scored 30 p...
articles.body:
Northern Arizona Lumberjacks (0-2) at Arizona Wildcats (1-1)

BOTTOM LINE: No. 5 Arizona hosts Northern Arizona after Motiejus Krivas scored 30 points in Arizona's 104-84 victory over the Cal Poly Mustangs.

articles.title: Usman Khawaja’s ‘Sandpapergate’ claims are ‘accurate’, says David Warner
articles.summary: ‘We’re not here to point fingers and we’re not opening old wounds,’ Australia’s Warner said of himself and Khawaja.
articles.body:
Former Australian cricketer David Warner has backed up claims made by former teammate Usman Khawaja, who said that their entire team had been aware ⁠⁠⁠⁠of the plan to ⁠⁠⁠⁠tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test tour of South Africa.

Warner spoke about the scandal, which continues to reverberate six years on, in a social media post on Monday, saying ‌‌‌‌that Khawaja’s comments were “100 percent accurate”.

The former Australian opener and fellow batters Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft were banned over the plan ⁠⁠⁠⁠to rough up the ball with sandpaper during the third Test at Newlands in Cape Town in 2018.

In a video posted on Instagram, Warner thanked Khawaja and said the investigation by Cricket Australia ‌‌‌‌into the incident was flawed.

“This whole interview process was rushed and botched,” added Warner, who retired from international cricket in 2024.

“Uzzie was sitting next to Cameron Bancroft. Uzzie was not interviewed. How is that a thorough investigation? It baffles me.”

In an excerpt from his autobiography released on Saturday, Khawaja said “open, lighthearted discussions” about tampering were not ⁠⁠⁠⁠confined to batters, bowlers or staff but extended throughout the team.

On Sunday, he added that he had chosen to speak about the ‘Sandpapergate’ scandal now after promising childhood friend Warner that he would share his side of the story.

Cricket Australia has not commented on the statement issued by Warner, who said that he and Khawaja were looking for accountability.

“We’re not here to point fingers and we’re not opening old wounds,” added the 40-year-old.

“It’s about accountability, transparency ⁠⁠⁠⁠and ensuring the truth is properly examined and perhaps it’s time people ⁠⁠⁠⁠stop scrutinising the person asking for accountability and start asking those responsible of the investigation to provide it.”

“Now, there was a lot of statements and inaccuracies over the last eight years that were put out in the media by people ⁠⁠⁠⁠and there were a lot of people who stayed silent,” Warner said.

Last week, Cricket Australia defended its 2018 probe which concluded that prior knowledge of the ⁠⁠⁠⁠plot was confined to Smith, Warner and Bancroft.

“All relevant information ⁠⁠⁠⁠presented to [Cricket Australia] to date has been properly considered and we remain comfortable with the findings of our integrity process,” it said in a statement on Saturday.

“There has been the ongoing opportunity to present any relevant information, and this remains the ‌‌‌‌case.”

The four Australian bowlers who played in the 2018 Test – Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon – issued a joint statement in 2021 denying any knowledge of the plot.

Cummins, now ‌‌‌‌the ‌‌‌‌Australian Test captain, said last month he had spoken with Khawaja about the upcoming release of his autobiography and dismissed suggestions that the book could trigger further fallout.

articles.title: Updated WWE Survivor Series 2026 Match Card Predictions Including The Bloodline vs. 946
articles.summary: WWE rolls into Houston and Daikin Park for its annual Thanksgiving weekend premium live event, Survivor Series, headlined by War Games.
articles.body:
WWE rolls into Houston and Daikin Park for its annual Thanksgiving weekend premium live event, Survivor Series, headlined by War Games.

While the main event is not yet official, all signs point to The Bloodline and 946 waging war in the marquee match.

What other matches should fans expect to see, and who will fill out the spots in those matches?

Find out with this preview of the Saturday, November 28 extravaganza.

Team USA (Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Chad Gable, Je'Von Evans, and Trick Williams) vs. Team Mexico (Penta, Rey Fenix, El Grande Americano, Dragon Lee, and Dominik Mysterio)

In the wake of his victory over Randy Orton at Crown Jewel, Cody Rhodes expressed his desire to captain Team USA against Team Mexico at Survivor Series, in the 5-on-5 Traditional Elimination Tag Team Match announced by Rey Mysterio on Friday.

Rhodes, CM Punk, Chad Gable, Je'Von Evans, and Trick Williams are all prominently featured Superstars with nothing else going on at this point for the premium live event in Houston.

Mysterio was careful not to mention AAA, thus the lack of those stars on the Mexican team. Penta and Rey Fenix have been all over WWE programming, Dragon Lee has built tremendous momentum for himself, El Grande Americano is the AAA Mega Champion, and the idea of Rey turning to his dastardly son to fill out the team provides some story background for the squad.

A fun, energetic, elimination tag team match the likes of which longtime WWE fans grew up with at the Survivor Series, this one would have the potential to steal the show and, potentially, set in motion WrestleMania 43 plans.

Team Charlotte (Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Bayley, and Rhea Ripley) vs. Team Jade (Jade Cargill, B-Fab, Michin, Fallon Henley, and Lainey Reid)

Charlotte Flair and Alexa Bliss have been feuding with Jade Cargill, Michin, B-Fab, and Fatal Influence in some form or fashion dating back to post-WrestleMania 42. Paxley, upon her arrival, joined the fray, too. Bayley was just introduced by way of a sneak attack by the former three on Raw.

It makes sense that those four women would team up to take on their rivals in the Women's War Game Match, but they would need a fifth to round out the field.

The Eradicator has a history of returning in time for this annual gimmick match. While we haven't been told that her injured knee has healed enough for her to return, this would be the perfect place for her to come back, given her history with the opposing team.

The match would have the history you expect from these War Games matches and, hopefully, be the rivalry's finale given how long it has been running.

If Ripley cannot go, another Raw star, such as Becky Lynch, would be a great addition and the story thread of her long, complicated history with Flair would make for hearty in-match storytelling potential.

Undisputed WWE Championship Match: Kevin Owens vs. Sami Zayn

Kevin Owens defeated CM Punk in their No Holds Barred Match on Friday's SmackDown and as a result, should earn a WWE Championship Match against his longtime friend Sami Zayn at Survivor Series.

The feud is one of the longest, most complex in modern WWE history, meaning the creative team does not have to get fancy or overbook any reasons for them to come together.

They have a history, Owens wants the title, Zayn has it...that's it.

That the match would likely be extraordinary, as most of their encounters are, only enhances the reason to bring those two together for a high-stakes title match at one of the most important premium live events of the year.

The Bloodline (Roman Reigns, Jacob Fatu, The Usos, and Solo Sikoa) vs. 946 (Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Cruz Montana, Bronco Nima, and Lucien Price)

From the moment Royce Keys and the 946 arrived on WWE TV, they have targeted The Bloodline. They have targeted The Usos, Jacob Fatu, and Solo Sikoa from day one, and recently, they have done the same to Roman Reigns after being humbled by The OTC in his first interaction with the group.

The young faction has been one step ahead of the family, introducing Jaida Parker, Carmelo Hayes, and Cruz Montana to the mix as they have built their group.

With Reigns having exorcised his demons in the form of challengers to his World Heavyweight Championship, and is fresh off a victory over Sami Zayn at Crown Jewel, he can refocus himself by leading The Usos, Sikoa, and a returning Fatu into war against their antagonists.

War Games, like the women's match, is the perfect culmination for a feud of this size. In a perfect world, the heels would go over to really establish them as a dangerous force in WWE but beating the Bloodline then creates the question: where do they go from here?

Considering how ingrained in WWE lore the babyface team is, it is a question WWE Creative probably is not ready to answer.

Reigns and Co. win here to wrap up this feud and turn their attention to WrestleMania. As for the heels? Hopefully, there is a plan for how to reinvigorate them post-Survivor Series.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Creed Brothers' Exit, Chelsea Reacts to Tiffany's Heel Turn, Je'Von Calls Out Troll
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Rumored Reaction to Creed Brothers' Release

While some WWE fans may have been caught off-guard by the Creed Brothers' release from the company last week, their co-workers reportedly didn't feel the same way.

Per Gene Mrosko of Cageside Seats, Bryan Alvarez said on Wrestling Observer Live that people within NXT "weren't surprised" about the Creed Brothers leaving WWE.

After it was discovered that the Creed Brothers were moved to the Alumni section of WWE's official website , Fightful Select confirmed that it appeared to be "a mutual parting of ways as their deal has expired."

Brutus and Julius Creed debuted in NXT in 2021 as part of Roderick Strong's Diamond Mine stable. They won the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic and the NXT Tag Team Championship the following year before being elevated to the main roster in 2023.

The Creeds were paired with Chad Gable during their main-roster run, first with Alpha Made and again during his Grande Americano as Los Americanos Hermanos. However, they never gained enough momentum to establish themselves on their own.

Still, the Creed Brothers are talented enough that they could make an impact in another promotion.

Chelsea Green Reacts to Tiffany Stratton's Heel Turn

Chelsea Green earned the biggest win of her career when she defeated Liv Morgan at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday, but her moment was overshadowed by Tiffany Stratton's betrayal.

After Green won the Women's Crown Jewel Championship, Stratton cashed in her Money in the Bank briefcase to take her WWE Women's Championship along with her newly won belt.

While speaking on the Crown Jewel post-show, Green admitted that losing her titles hurt even more because of how Stratton turned on her.

"How do you think I feel? I spent my entire wrestling career waiting for this moment, wanting to stand here and tell the WWE Universe, and my mom and dad, and my friends that I belong here," Green said (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News). "I just spent 10 minutes on SmackDown telling the world that this was going to be the moment at Crown Jewel that was gonna show everyone I belonged here. And instead, I didn't just lose my championship — I lost a friend."

Green added that she would try to bounce back, but it was clear that Stratton's betrayal still stung.

"So, I'm gonna go home and regroup," she said. "And I'm gonna do whatever I need to do to build my confidence back up."

After teaming with Penta and defeating Bron Breakker and Austin Theory to become the new World Tag Team Champions at WWE Crown Jewel on Saturday, Je'Von Evans couldn't help but laugh off his haters.

Evans took to social media to fire back at a troll who previously called him out for getting a title shot.

After the user wrote, "JeVon Evans has won ZERO #WWE titles. WTF is his scrawny ass doing in the world title picture?!" Evans reposted the tweet with a few laughing emojis and a picture of his new belt:

Evans had long been considered a future champion in WWE. At just 22 years old, he's already become one of the most exciting Superstars on the main roster.

Evans' partnership with Penta will propel him to bigger opportunities as the new tag team champs begin their reign atop the division.

articles.title: Re-Ranking the Top 10 2027 NHL Free Agents After Nikita Kucherov's Trade Request
articles.summary: On Oct. 30, the hockey world was stunned to learn that superstar winger Nikita Kucherov had requested a trade after deciding not to sign a contract extension with the Tampa Bay Lightning.
articles.body:
On Oct. 30, the hockey world was stunned to learn that superstar winger Nikita Kucherov had requested a trade after deciding not to sign a contract extension with the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Kucherov, 33, is in the final season of his eight-year contract worth an average annual value of $9.5 million. The reigning Hart Memorial Trophy winner is slated to become an unrestricted free agent on July 1 and would be the top player if he goes to market.

The Lightning released a statement saying they weren't trading Kucherov, but pundits speculated they could change their minds before the March 1 trade deadline. He has a 10-team trade list, but it's currently unknown which teams are on it.

If Kucherov is traded to a new team and signs an extension before July 1, it would further shrink a UFA market already depleted by the off-season extensions signed by Colorado Avalanche defenseman Cale Makar, Vegas Golden Knights winger Mark Stone, and Detroit Red Wings forward Alex DeBrincat.

We last examined the best players slated for free agency in 2027 on July 2 . Given what's transpired since, we felt it was time to re-rank the top 10 UFA-eligible players.

Next summer's UFA market is thin on quality starting goaltenders. Most are now in their mid-to-late thirties with their best seasons behind them.

The same can be said of Jordan Binnington, who turns 34 next July 11. He backstopped the St. Louis Blues to the Stanley Cup in 2019, which helped him land a six-year deal worth an average annual value of $6 million.

Since then, Binnington has struggled with consistency and never regained the heights of 2018-19. However, he proved capable of clutch goaltending during international competition, helping Canada win the 4 Nations Face-Off in 2025 and reach the Gold Medal Game at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

A playoff contender with Stanley Cup aspirations seeking experienced goaltending depth could consider Binnington a worthwhile gamble on an affordable short-term deal.

Artturi Lehkonen doesn't put up points like his linemates Nathan MacKinnon and Martin Necas. However, the 31-year-old winger's hard-working, two-way style of play has made him a valuable member of the Avalanche's first line .

Lehkonen's game often comes with a physical price. Despite his injury history, he's put up solid numbers, exceeding 20-plus goals and 45-plus points in three of the last four seasons. He's on pace for a career-best season, leading the Avalanche with 12 goals in 18 games this season.

It's unlikely that Lehkonen can maintain that production, but his overall game would make him a highly sought-after player in next summer's UFA market. He also has Stanley Cup experience, winning with the Avs in 2022 and reaching the Cup Final in 2021 with the Montreal Canadiens.

Lehkonen is in the final season of a five-year contract worth an average annual value of $4.5 million. He could receive a significant raise on his next deal, especially if he becomes available in next summer's free-agent market.

An original member of the Kraken, Vince Dunn has been an invaluable defenseman since the team selected him in the 2021 expansion draft. They will try to convince the 30-year-old left-shot blueliner to sign a contract extension.

Dunn is in the final season of a four-year deal worth an average annual value of $7.4 million. He and defense partner Adam Larsson have been an effective top pairing on the Kraken's blue line.

A mobile puck-moving defenseman, Dunn currently logs over 23 minutes of ice time per game . He also sees time on their special teams. The 6'0, 200-pounder netted 35-plus points in each of the past five seasons, including a career-high 64 points in 2022-23.

Dunn is an alternate captain with the Kraken and also has a championship pedigree, having won the Stanley Cup with the St. Louis Blues in 2019. His leadership, Cup experience, and big-minute game will draw teams looking to bolster the left side of their defense corps.

Terrible Contracts Teams Wish They Could Dump 🤦‍♂️

It's been over seven years since Ryan O'Reilly was at the peak of his career. In 2018-19, he had a career-high 77 points and won the Frank J. Selke Trophy as the league's best defensive forward during the regular season. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy , leading the St. Louis Blues to the Stanley Cup.

O'Reilly's production and performance slowly declined after that, but he bounced back with a 74-point effort with the Nashville Predators last season. The 35-year-old center is currently among the Predators' leading scorers with 17 points in as many games.

Now in his 18th NHL campaign, O'Reilly remains well-respected as a two-way center. Given his skills and experience, he shouldn't have any difficulty landing with another team if he doesn't re-sign with the Predators.

O'Reilly is in the final season of a four-year contract worth an affordable $4.5 million. Teams might be willing to give him a pay bump on his next deal, though it could be for two or three years.

At 36, Erik Karlsson is at the age when a player's best seasons are usually well behind them. While he won't reach the heights that made him the only active three-time winner of the James Norris Memorial Trophy , his puck-moving skills and experience should make him an intriguing free-agent target next summer.

Karlsson is in the final season of an eight-year, $92 million contract with an average annual value of $11.5 million. He'll never make that kind of money again, but he could be a worthwhile addition for teams seeking a veteran right-shot blueliner on a shorter, less expensive deal.

After struggling through his first two seasons with the Penguins, Karlsson improved last season under head coach Dan Muse with 66 points in 75 games. He currently leads the struggling Penguins with 17 points in as many games.

Karlsson is still seeking his first Stanley Cup championship. He could be a solid addition to a contender, especially if paired with a reliable defensive-minded blueliner.

Teams in the market for a big, versatile, two-way center will beat a path to Pavel Zacha's door if he's available on July 1. The 6'4", 212-pounder is in the final season of a four-year contract with an average annual value of $4.8 million.

Zacha, 29, is a top-six forward who can play center or wing. After six sometimes difficult seasons with the New Jersey Devils, he came into his own with the Bruins. He's had 57-plus points in three of the last four seasons and is on pace for similar stats this season .

The Bruins reportedly want to re-sign Zacha. However, the resurgence of veteran Elias Lindholm and the promising improvement of young centers Fraser Minten, James Hagens, and Matthew Poitras could make him the odd man out if he proves too expensive to retain.

Given the limited number of quality centers in the trade market, Zacha won't have any difficulty finding a new team if he becomes available on July 1. He could double his money on his next contract.

The greatest player of his era, Sidney Crosby is in the final season of a two-year deal worth an average annual value of $8.7 million. He's spent his entire 22-season NHL career with the Pittsburgh Penguins, and it's expected he'll re-sign with them if he decides to continue his career.

However, the Penguins have been retooling their roster since 2022-23, resulting in only one playoff appearance during that time . Another missed postseason could tempt the 39-year-old Crosby to test the market to see which team will give him the best shot at one more Stanley Cup run.

Crosby has shown signs of slowing down, but he remains the league's most respected player. His skilled playmaking, championship pedigree, two-way skills, and leadership make him an irresistible free-agent option for clubs with Stanley Cup aspirations.

We again stress that Crosby is more likely to stick with the Penguins if he decides to continue his career for another season. Nevertheless, it would be fun to see which clubs would get into the bidding if he went to market on July 1.

Nikita Kucherov's potential absence from next summer's UFA market automatically makes Jason Robertson the top forward available if he doesn't re-sign with the Dallas Stars. He's on a one-year, $12 million contract .

A long, sometimes contentious negotiation process led to Robertson getting that deal from the cap-strapped Stars. At one point, he was nearly traded to the Seattle Kraken in June, but his refusal to sign a long-term deal worth $15 million annually scuttled that deal.

Since his full-time rookie season in 2020-21, Robertson has led the Stars with 222 goals and 286 assists for 508 points in 470 games. He's netted at least 80 points in each of the last four seasons, including a career-best 109 points in 2022-23.

An elite scoring winger, Robertson could land a long-term contract worth over $20 million annually if he goes to market next summer. His offensive skills mean he won't be available for long.

If Nikita Kucherov isn't available on July 1, Quinn Hughes will become the top player in next summer's UFA market. The 27-year-old defenseman is in the final season of a six-year contract worth an average annual value of $7.9 million.

Since his rookie season in 2019-20, Hughes ranks second to Colorado's Cale Makar with 508 total points (as of Nov. 8). He's had at least 76 points in each of the last four seasons, including a career-high 92-point performance in 2023-24 that earned him the James Norris Memorial Trophy .

An elite offensive defenseman, Hughes' puck movement, reliable production, and his underrated defensive play should earn him a long-term contract with an average annual value comparable to Makar's $20.4 million starting in 2027-28.

The Wild hope to re-sign Hughes, especially after giving up three top prospects and a first-rounder to acquire him from the Vancouver Canucks. However, he remains coy about his future, and the longstanding rumors that he hopes to reunite with his brothers (Jack and Luke) in New Jersey persist.

As we noted in the introduction, unless the Tampa Bay Lightning trade Nikita Kucherov before July 1, he'll be the top player in next summer's UFA market.

The awards alone speak for themselves. He's played on two Stanley Cup champions with the Lightning. He's taken home the Art Ross Trophy three times and is a two-time winner of the Hart Memorial Trophy and the Ted Lindsay Award .

His stats also make the case. Since his debut in 2013-14, he's been the third-most prolific NHL scorer with 1,146 points. He's also the points leader (177) among all postseason scorers during that stretch.

Kucherov reportedly seeks $20 million annually on a six-year contract. The Lightning appear reluctant to invest that much in a player who'll be 34 next June. However, if they won't pay it, other clubs happily will.

Stats and trophy info via NHL.com . Salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: Ranking WWE's 10 Biggest Winners and Losers Since WrestleMania 42
articles.summary: It has been a whirlwind of a year for WWE, with several Superstars breaking out and ascending to new levels of super stardom.
articles.body:
It has been a whirlwind of a year for WWE, with several Superstars breaking out and ascending to new levels of super stardom.

While the week-to-week product hasn't been consistently strong throughout 2026, that hasn't stopped some from putting forth their best work both in the ring and on the mic. It's also been a banner year in terms of fresh faces rising in the ranks and establishing themselves as future world champs.

The booking hasn't been kind to everyone on the roster, however, as others have struggled to either make gains or have fallen far from where they once were. The vast number of injuries WWE has had this year hasn't helped, nor have the questionable decisions made by those in charge.

It's especially astounding to see where certain competitors were around WrestleMania 42 time and the string of setbacks they've suffered since then. Wins and losses go beyond match outcomes; it's all about how prominently they're featured, their direction and how highly officials view them.

These are WWE's biggest winners and losers since 'Mania, ranked.

10. Winner: Danhausen, Loser: Chelsea Green

Danhausen and Chelsea Green will never be mistaken for being masters of the squared circle, but as entertaining characters, they are both invaluable assets to WWE TV.

Danhausen has been one of WWE's smartest hires all year. He isn't an in-ring regular nor should he be, but in addition to being a self-marketing machine, he's made the most of everything he's been involved in, and is a prime example of why variety in wrestling is so important.

His matches haven't been anything to write home about, but it is worth noting that he has remained undefeated in one-on-one competition, including racking up a victory over Dominik Mysterio at SummerSlam. He's also been at war with Gunther in recent months.

Green loses more often than she wins yet is one of WWE's biggest overachievers of all-time. This year alone, she's held both the Women's United States Championship and the WWE Women's Championship.

Unfortunately, it was clear from how she was portrayed during her three-month title reign that she was never intended to be the face of SmackDown's women's division, resulting in a run that will be looked back on as being lackluster. Whether she'll ultimately be elevated and stay in that spot is unknown, but time will tell.

9. Winner: Royce Keys, Loser: Carmelo Hayes

Fresh off his departure from AEW, Royce Keys made an immediate impact in his Royal Rumble debut and went on to win the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal. He was practically nonexistent on WWE TV prior to WrestleMania 42 but has been a regular on Raw and SmackDown since then.

His run-ins with The Bloodline led to him creating his own group in The 946 and enlisting the likes of OTM, Jaida Parker, Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana. His matches might be far and few between, but they've been firmly established as the most dominant force on the flagship show, with a WarGames match against The Bloodline obviously on the horizon.

Speaking of Hayes, although he's been back on the right track as part of The 946, his 2026 as a whole hasn't been stellar, particularly post-WrestleMania 42. He ripped it up on Friday nights as United States champion for the first three months of the year before disappearing entirely after dropping the belt right before 'Mania.

He was then M.I.A. for almost the entire summer on SmackDown outside of an unsuccessful United States title bout with Baron Corbin in August. Again, his stock has since recovered now that he's in the top heel faction on Raw, but it was mostly a waste of a year for him prior to that point.

8. Winner: Liv Morgan, Loser: Jacob Fatu

Liv Morgan emerged as one of the anchors of WWE's women's division in 2024 and has yet to be usurped from that spot.

WrestleMania 42 marked her return to the top of the mountain when she kicked off her second reign with the Women's World Championship. It's been well documented that she barely defended the title in the months that followed, but she was an important part of the program, nonetheless.

She scored a big win over Iyo Sky at SummerSlam before losing the belt back to Stephanie Vaquer a Chile live event. Morgan shockingly regained the gold mere weeks later at Money in the Bank and should remain at the helm of Raw's women's scene for the foreseeable future.

Jacob Fatu also finds himself in a prominent position on Raw right now, but he's lost a considerable amount of momentum since WrestleMania when he was a one-man wrecking machine in his rivalry with Drew McIntyre.

Fatu should have won a world title in the wake of WrestleMania but was instead relegated to losing to Roman Reigns twice and then having to rejoin The Bloodline. Perhaps he will break away from the faction in the coming months, but there was no reason to interrupt his hot streak in the first place.

Following an injury layoff, Chad Gable resurfaced in the Royal Rumble with his El Grande Americano gimmick and kicked off a feud with the new Americano that felt like it'd never end, at least on the main roster.

That said, the grand blow-off to their feud exceeded all expectations and was one of the best bouts in WWE all year. The company wisely capitalized on that momentum for Gable by having him revert to his original moniker and enter Intercontinental Championship contention.

Upon winning the title from Penta at SummerSlam, he was determined to be a fighting champ and did not disappoint. His three-month reign saw him have weekly bangers with the red brand's midcard and showcase his skills in a way he never has before on his own in WWE.

Gunther should be having similar quality matches, but he's largely been spinning his wheels this year and failing to be a part of anything remotely memorable. His short-lived storyline with Nick Aldis during SummerSlam season was superb, but everything he's done (or not done) has been terribly unimpressive for a former world champion.

The Ring General can be a main event player again in no time, but his booking this year has left a lot to be desired, and has been especially underwhelming considering he retired John Cena last December and AJ Styles not long after.

6. Winner: Trick Williams, Loser: Jey Uso

There can be no question that WWE has nailed Trick Williams' main roster call-up, and that he's well on his way toward winning a world championship.

His United States Championship victory at WrestleMania 42 led him to knocking off everyone who stepped up to challenge him including Sami Zayn, Ricky Saints and The Miz. Baron Corbin briefly put a pause to his reign before it resumed at Sunday Night's Main Event in early September.

He's recently rekindled his rivalry with Zayn, this time over the Undisputed WWE title. He's still improving in the ring, but he's already over with the audience and is rightfully being booked as the star he is.

Jey Uso once found himself in a similar spot with fans a year or two ago, whereas now he's a glorified tag team wrestler and a Bloodline lackey at best.

The Usos have been sidekicks for Roman Reigns since WrestleMania 42. Although Jey advanced all the way to the finals of the King of the Ring tournament, nothing else he's done during this stretch would make you think that he was once the World Heavyweight champion.

Say what you will about CM Punk not being quite as crisp in the ring as he used to be, but even at age 48, the guy can still very much go and is one of the most must-see aspects of SmackDown each week.

He left WrestleMania 42 without the World Heavyweight Championship but instantly captured the Undisputed WWE Championship on returning on Raw in Chicago this past July. He proceeded to have a terrific two-month reign that featured title defenses against Cody Rhodes, Kevin Owens and Johnny Gargano.

Punk lost the belt to Sami Zayn in September, but his unrelenting rivalry with Owens and their pursuit of the prestigious prize has kept them busy. He's won his fair share of matches while putting over a number of others simultaneously.

LA Knight challenged for a world title this year, too, but unlike The Second City Saint, Knight lost when it mattered most at Money in the Bank. WWE was doing a perfectly fine job with him between WrestleMania and SummerSlam, but his constant high-profile losses have hurt whatever shred of credibility he had left.

A heel turn might be the only way Knight can be salvaged at this point, because there really isn't anywhere for him to go from here but down if he doesn't.

Penta's 2025 was all about him establishing a connection with the WWE audience and getting fans familiar with what he can do. In 2026, he's worked his way up the ladder and has won a few titles along the way.

Penta spent the WrestleMania 42 to SummerSlam stretch holding the Intercontinental Championship and having a standout reign. WWE wasted no time in elevating him to the next level as soon as he dropped that title, as he then had an instant classic with Roman Reigns in Mexico for the belt.

Within weeks of that night, he became Mr. Money in the Bank to guarantee himself another opportunity at a world title in the future and won the World Tag Team Championship with Je'Von Evans.

Ricky Saints has had the opposite luck in that he can't seem to buy a victory since joining SmackDown earlier this year.

He's a natural fit for the blue brand, but he was quickly eliminated from United States Championship contention and has lost against Rey Fenix at every turn as of late. It isn't impossible for him to rebound, but he'll need to be supported by the booking for sure.

3. Winner: Sami Zayn, Loser: Jade Cargill

Everything about Sami Zayn's character this year has been so beautifully organic that it's truly brought the best out of him as a performer.

That wasn't the case just prior to WrestleMania 42 when fans were booing him winning back the United States Championship. His loss of the title to Trick Williams was the catalyst for his descent into madness and not only earned him a long-deserved spot in SmackDown's main event scene but also a run with the Undisputed WWE Championship.

Although it only lasted nine days, he refused to stay down for long and eventually regained the prestigious prize in September. Zayn has found a way to win in a majority of his matches, and while he once again fell short against Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel, he was endorsed and "acknowledged" by The Tribal Chief afterward.

Jade Cargill's television time has hardly been curtailed his year, but she's not as feared of a force as she was when she was WWE Women's champion going into WrestleMania 42.

She lost championship rematches with Rhea Ripley and Tiffany Stratton in the subsequent months and hasn't been able to get the better of Charlotte Flair. She's won her fair share of inconsequential matches but hasn't been able to get anything going in some time.

This is the least special Cargill has felt since signing with WWE three years ago. Her feud with Flair has been as basic as can be, so WWE needs to figure something out fast as far as what can be done to make her an attraction again.

2. Winner: Oba Femi, Loser: Bron Breakker

Bron Breakker and Oba Femi are the future faces of WWE, but they're both in drastically different positions because of how they've been booked in 2026.

Much like Trick Williams, Femi has been a can't-miss prospect for WWE since being called up to the main roster at the onset of the year. It was evident that greatness was in store for him as soon as he scored that swift win over Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, and he hasn't slowed down since then.

From becoming King of the Ring to retiring Lesnar inside Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam, WWE has practically done everything right with Femi other than have him challenge for and win the World Heavyweight Championship. He's also systematically taken down The Vision to keep himself busy.

The Vision's demise should be a positive sign for Breakker, who outgrew the group when he betrayed Seth Rollins and set his sights on the world title. An injury sidelined him from this year's Road to WrestleMania, but other than that, his lack of luck has completely been the fault of WWE Creative.

Breakker has been an afterthought in the worst way possible this year and desperately needs to get back to what made him a hot commodity at this time a year ago.

1. Winner: Roman Reigns, Loser: Dominik Mysterio

Roman Reigns being considered WWE's biggest winner of 2026 shouldn't be shocking in the slightest, but to his credit, he has stepped up his game this year to a significant degree and has been on fire as World Heavyweight champion.

The concern with Reigns from fans at this stage of his career is whether he can appear enough to justify holding the gold. Amazingly, he's been around much more this year and has so far totaled five title defenses and a Men's Crown Jewel Championship win over Sami Zayn.

The Bloodline being back in full form has played a pivotal in his resurgence this year, but at least the stable hasn't factored into many if any of Reigns' matches since WrestleMania 42.

Dominik Mysterio, on the other hand, couldn't be further from being considered a world championship-caliber competitor, at least based on how he's been booked throughout 2026.

His loss of the Intercontinental Championship prior to WrestleMania was merely the tip of the iceberg, as he went on to suffer from a lack of direction for many months before losing to Danhausen at SummerSlam. Dropping the AAA Mega Championship in September should have freed him up for bigger and better things, but being omitted from the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match wasn't a positive indicator of where he was headed.

He's mostly been left to wither away in the midcard until the WWE brass wake up and realize the potential they've been wasting with Mysterio in 2026. He has his entire career ahead of him at 29, but it's unnecessary for him to have to wait any longer to get his just due.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Capitán Navarro
articles.summary: La opinión de Alberto Bote.
articles.body: ¡Oh, capitán, mi capitán! Es la primera frase que se me vino a la cabeza tras ver a España campeona del mundo el pasado sábado viendo a Paquito Navarro celebrar en la central del Khalifa Stadium en su última participación con la camiseta de España. La célebre referencia a la película 'El club de los poetas muertos' en la que un profesor interpretado por Robin Williams despierta el interés de sus alumnos en la poesía con una moraleja de fondo que refleja, primero, la persecución de los sueños; y después, el valor de aquellos que guían el camino y que aún cayendo al alcanzar la meta, su legado debe haber servido a una causa mayor: el bien común. Y ese es el sentido que mejor se ajusta a la envergadura de la figura de Paquito con España. Desde su pueril debut en 2008 en Calgary (Canadá) ha sido campeón en cuatro ocasiones (2008, 2010, 2021 y 2026), ha perdido más que ha ganado, ni que decir tiene que ha vivido, quizá, la derrota más dolorosa de su carrera en la final de Cascais 2016 cuando rozó el título junto a Juan Martín Díaz y también ha sabido liderar de muchas y diferentes formas, dentro y fuera de pista, una transición cuando el pádel español no era ni parecido al que ahora domina el ranking. La palabra capitán ha sido el sello personal del sevillano con España casi, casi, desde el principio. Con 18 años debutó y desde entonces ha sido un fijo en las convocatorias para primero secundar a las estrellas del momento, aprender por el camino y después asumir la responsabilidad de capitanear en las buenas y en las que no. Lo hizo en Doha 2021, calambres incluídos, definiendo junto a Lebrón para devolver a España la corona 11 años y cuatro ediciones después; también remontando con ‘El Lobo’ en el 2022 a Tapia y Chingotto y viendo como el punto no servía para campeonar; o en el 2024 protagonizando la derrota en el tercer partido junto a Mike Yanguas frente a unos inesperados Augsburger y Libaak. Y lo ha vuelto a hacer en su despedida. Con España sorprendiendo a Argentina en el primer punto Paquito saltó a pista con la difícil labor de intentar junto a Jon Sanz dar la sorpresa ante los cabezas de cartel de la albiceleste, Tapia y Chingotto. Sí, otra vez. Pero en esta ocasión no solo no lograría la remontada sino que recibiría un duro castigo cayendo en 55 minutos y haciendo apenas tres juegos. “Me he comido la paliza más bonita de mi vida”, afirmaba el sevillano en rueda de prensa tras salir España campeona hace apenas unos días en una clara alusión a que, para él, el bien colectivo primaba por encima de los egos personales. Y, claro, es evidente que ser campeón lo tapa todo, pero hay que estar hecho de una pasta diferente para vivir un instante así de amargo cuando uno cuelga la camiseta nacional como el jugador más laureado de la historia de España. Paquito se retira y lo hace como el jugador más ganador, pero este es un hito que muy probablemente pierda y rápido porque los Coello, Galán, Lebrón o Coki tienen carrera y futuro para poder alcanzar o superar una marca que no se antoja insalvable. Pero 'Pacquiao' se retira con el indudable honor de haber sido el jugador más importante en la historia de España aunque no acabe siendo el mejor, el más ganador o el más determinante. La influencia de Navarro va más allá de los títulos, su valor reside en haber sabido liderar su deporte tejiendo un puente entre dos generaciones del pádel español para hacer de La Roja una selección sin complejos y, a la par, una familia. Y lo hizo de forma poco ortodoxa, lejos de ser perfecto o ejemplar, pero como Jon Keating en la ya citada película de 1989 (año en el que él nació, por cierto) inspirando a aquellos que le acompañaron a que había algo más allá o dando valor un cuestionado Juanjo Gutiérrez. Y su despedida de la Selección, con sus compañeros cantando al unísono “Paquito quédate, Paquito quédate” en rueda de prensa es la representación perfecta de la emblemática escena con la que arrancaba esta columna de opinión, el momento culmen en el que los alumnos rinden homenaje al líder caído, se suben a los pupitres y se despiden con un balsámico: ¡Oh, capitán, mi capitán!.

articles.title: British-Somali ‌‌‌‌boxer Ramla Ali defeats Mikiah Kreps for first ⁠⁠⁠⁠world title
articles.summary: Ali wins a controversial split-decision fight against American Kreps to claim IBO and WBF junior featherweight belts.
articles.body:
Ramla Ali, a British Somali boxer whose life story is the subject of a new film, has realised a long-held dream and won her first world title to claim two vacant junior featherweight belts in the United States.

The 36-year-old landed the biggest titles of her career by winning the IBO and WBF belts in a controversial split-decision victory over American fighter Mikiah Kreps in Arlington, Texas, on Sunday.

The nail-biting nature of the 10-round contest should not have come as too much of a surprise, as the duo are former sparring partners and ended the night with an expression of mutual respect.

“Mikiah, I want to share this victory with you because you pushed me for 10 rounds,” an emotional Ali said while addressing her opponent, who she stopped from exiting the ring after being declared the winner.

“I kept saying I’m so tired because your work rate was next level. I don’t know how I kept up, so thank you for being such a great boxer.”

The 30-year-old Niagara Falls native reciprocated the emotion. “I respect you,” Kreps said as both fighters wrapped an arm around each other.

During the fight, Ali had Kreps on the canvas in round three, but she was behind her younger opponent in the overall punch count at the end of the fight.

The outcome of the fight caused controversy from the moment the referee lifted Ali’s arm when the decision was announced.

According to the official punch statistics from the fight, Kreps outlanded Ali by 115 blows to 78 and the American was also way ahead in the power shot count.

One judge scored the bout 98-91 for Kreps but the other judges saw the fight differently and gave Ali the win with scores of 97-92 and 96-93.

Veteran promoter Lou Di Bella wrote on social media, “Mikiah Kreps won that fight and it wasn’t even close. Stevie Wonder could see that.”

From Somalia’s civil war to world champion

The external noise would have mattered little to Ali, who dropped to her knees when the scores were announced.

Ali and her family are no strangers to adversity, having settled in London in 1992 after fleeing Somalia during its civil war.

Years after picking up the sport as a teenager in East London, Ali became the first Somali boxer to compete at the Olympic Games when she represented the country of her birth at Tokyo 2020. She later became the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title.

Ali’s journey has provided the inspiration for the movie ‘In the Shadows’ starring Top Boy actor Jasmine Jobson.

The fighter lost her father earlier this year and said she stayed up all night prior to the fight, wishing he would have been around to see her in the ring.

“My father passed away in May, so I was really emotional,” she said in a post-fight interview with All The Smoke Boxing.

“Every round, I kept going to my corner to tell my coach I couldn’t do it any more because I was physically exhausted. I boxed through my skin and I’m glad I got the victory.”

Ali’s career has always been multi-dimensional. As a model and UNICEF ambassador, she has projected her voice beyond sporting arenas.

“I can’t put into words what this means to me and what this means to all of Somalia,” she said, fighting back tears, while standing inside the ring.

“I’ve hopefully inspired so many young girls and boys out there to dream big and that’s all I’ve ever wanted to do.”

articles.title: La niña prodigio del ajedrez, gran protagonista del IX Festival Internacional Salamanca
articles.standfirst: La inglesa Bodhana Sivanandan, con sólo 11 años, está batiendo todos los registros de precocidad de un mito del ajedrez como la húngara Judit Polgar
articles.summary: La inglesa Bodhana Sivanandan, con sólo 11 años, está batiendo todos los registros de precocidad de un mito del ajedrez como la húngara Judit Polgar
articles.body: La nueva reina del ajedrez, la inglesa Bodhana Sivanandan, la mujer que con sólo 11 años está batiendo todos los registros de precocidad de un mito del ajedrez como la húngara Judit Polgar, será la gran protagonista deportiva del IX Festival Internacional Salamanca Cuna del Ajedrez Moderno que se celebrará desde el miércoles y hasta el próximo sábado en el Centro Internacional del Español (CIE). Corría el año 1989 y una niña pelirroja de 13 años, Judit Polgar, acudió junto con su hermana Susan a disputar el torneo de Salamanca. Era, pese a su juventud, una de las favoritas, pero los resultados no terminaron acompañándole y concluyó en la 12ª posición. Su transcendencia en el ajedrez ha sido tal -series, documentales y libros en todos los idiomas- que sirva como curiosidad que el Ayuntamiento de Salamanca organiza en la actualidad talleres educativos y familiares con el nombre de Judit Polgar en la Casa de la Mujer. Mañana, con dos años menos que la campeona magyar, Bodhana Sivanandan caminará por su misma senda y tratará de seguir haciendo historia en la ciudad en la que Luis Ramírez de Lucena compiló las reglas del ajedrez moderno en 1497, en el incunable Repetición de amores y arte de ajedrez, el tratado impreso más antiguo que se conserva en el mundo. Un libro del que se conservan muy pocos ejemplares, uno de ellos en perfecto estado en la biblioteca de la Universidad de Salamanca. Sivanandan, la Gran Maestro femenina más joven de la historia y que ostenta también el título de Maestro Internacional masculino (abierto), se medirá en Salamanca a jugadores de mucho mayor nivel de los que lo hizo en su día la menor de la saga Polgar, como el español Francisco Vallejo, excampeón del mundo sub-18 y pentacampeón de España absoluto, que después de unos meses de inactividad vuelve a la competición. El neerlandés Loek van Wely, antiguo top-10 mundial y ocho veces campeón de los Países Bajos, el peruano José Eduardo Martínez Alcántara y la alemana Elisabeth Pähtz, primera mujer de su país con el título de Gran Maestro absoluto (2022) y la ucraniana Anastasiia Hnatyshyn, de 15 años, campeona de Europa femenina en 2026, completan la nómina del torneo diseñado por el director técnico de la competición Amador González de la Nava. La prueba se disputa por sistema de liga a doble vuelta (10 rondas) en la modalidad de partidas de 30 minutos más 5 segundos adicionales por movimiento. La entrada es gratuita y hay una sala de comentarios anexa con comentarios a cargo del Gran Maestro Alfonso Romero El festival, organizado por el Ayuntamiento de Salamanca, la Universidad de Salamanca y Alumni, con el apoyo de la Junta de Castilla y León, aúna deporte de élite y promoción con cultura. Entre las actividades paralelas, hay que destacar las partidas simultáneas que se celebrarán mañana en el CIE y el torneo relámpago que tendrá lugar el viernes en el Centro Gallego. También, las conferencias del laureado árbitro internacional y organizador Joaquín Espejo (“Mis vivencias con Veselin Topalov”) y de la artista multidisciplinar Nistal Mayorga (“64 miradas”), quien expondrá sus tres series al óleo y acuarela de los retratos de algunos jugadores que han participado en ediciones anteriores del Festival.
