articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: How Rob Hawkins overcame illness to propel England towards World Cup glory
articles.summary: When Rob Hawkins replied to what he thought was an advert to play wheelchair basketball in 2014 he could not have imagined he would be a key part of an England side defending their Rugby League World Cup title.
articles.body:
When Rob Hawkins replied to what he thought was an advert to play wheelchair basketball more than a decade ago he could not have imagined he would be a key part of an England side defending their Rugby League World Cup title.

While the men's and women's teams have already returned home, England face Australia in Wollongong on Tuesday (08:45 GMT) in the semi-finals of the Wheelchair competition, aiming to take another step towards becoming the first nation to lift the trophy on three occasions.

However, 25-year-old Hawkins, who was a big presence in the side to triumph in Manchester four years ago , has also had to overcome the odds - and a battle with chronic fatigue syndrome - to become one of the stars of the international game.

The England and Halifax Panthers wing only took up rugby league in 2014 after being bedbound for 18 months, and following a quirk of fate.

"Before my condition I was very sporting and athletic. I'd been doing running, football, started getting into other sports like rugby league and so I wanted to try and find something that interested me," Hawkins told BBC Sport.

"I saw something on television about wheelchair basketball so we tried looking for our local club, and what we thought was Halifax wheelchair basketball. When we went to a session it turned out it was wheelchair rugby league instead.

"I thought I'd give it a try and see what I thought. I jumped into a chair for about 20 minutes before my body probably wouldn't let me continue any more and I just kept wanting to go back and get better. It was definitely an interesting turn of events but I don't regret any minute of staying in the sport.

"When I found out that I could play internationally it kind of drove my competitiveness back out that I didn't have since before the condition."

Hawkins won the coveted IRL Golden Boot Award in 2024 and 2025 after being voted the International Wheelchair Player of the Year.

He is also Super League's reigning Wheels of Steel winner, given to the best player in the competition.

Yet it did not always come so easy. His condition previously meant that he had to use walking frames or rely on family members just to get to the toilet, and he also missed two years of learning at high school.

"There are still times where I just need that extra rest," he added.

"There are days where I still go down and I do just rest all day long. The thing that I've just learned over the years is effectively just trying to pace myself as much as I can.

"It feels weird to say - I'm happy I've had this condition because it's taught me and seemed to show me a different aspect of life where I've actually connected with people that I might not have done previously."

USA NS Pacific Islands to host 2030 World Cup

The England team who can still win the Rugby League World Cup

England aim to paint another step on ladder

England go into their semi-final against hosts Australia as favourites to reach the showpiece match.

They followed a 98-18 victory over Wales with a 134-0 win against the USA before defeating Ireland 68-32 to top Pool A.

Australia claimed thumping wins over New Zealand and Scotland before their momentum was checked by a 69-34 loss to France, who were runners-up four years ago.

However, having pushed England close in the 2025 Ashes, Hawkins says that while England will not underestimate their opponents, they are relishing the challenge in front of them.

"I'm excited for the pressure," Hawkins added.

"We know they have been bringing a decent crowd in and that it is going to be a difficult game with the atmosphere and with the team that we're facing, but we also know that we are confident to basically go and do our game and stick to our game plan as well.

"We have some ladders in our team room and every game that we've won so far we've been spray painting it gold.

"We're just taking that one step up the ladder every time - we're just looking forward to facing Australia."

Paul Williams scored five tries as Wales eased past New Zealand 64-36 to reach the fifth-place play-off final.

Captain Jodie Boyd-Ward also celebrated becoming the first player in Wheelchair World Cup history to reach 50 caps with two tries of her own.

Wales will now face Scotland in Wollongong on Thursday in their final game.

articles.title: El Manchester United busca líder
articles.standfirst: William Hill sitúa a Eddie Howe como principal favorito
articles.summary: William Hill sitúa a Eddie Howe como principal favorito
articles.body: El Manchester United vuelve a mirar al banquillo. Con Michael Carrick pendiente de una decisión que podría tomarse durante el parón de selecciones de noviembre, tras dos actuaciones que no han convencido a nadie en Old Trafford, el mercado de apuestas deportivas ya ha movido ficha. William Hill tiene claro quién lidera la carrera, aunque en las últimas horas el panorama ha cambiado de forma notable. Asimismo, 3 de cada 4 usuarios de Oddschecker sitúan al United perdiendo la categoría y jugando en Championship la próxima temporada. El pánico, la racha negativa y la crisis deportiva en Old Trafford acaparan la mayoría del flujo de registros. El principal candidato para darle la vuelta a la situación es Eddie Howe, con una cuota de 2.88. El técnico, sin equipo tras su salida del Newcastle, con el que ganó la Carabao Cup, encarna mejor que nadie la filosofía de INEOS. Aun así, su precio ha vivido un vaivén llamativo. La razón de ese movimiento en las casas de apuestas tiene nombre y apellido: Mauricio Pochettino, a cuota 3. El argentino, que dirige a la selección de Estados Unidos y renovó su contrato hace poco, se ha convertido en la gran sorpresa del mercado, tras pasar de ser un candidato casi descartado, con cuotas de 33 a 1, a colocarse como segunda opción en cuestión de días. Es un nombre que no deja de aparecer cada vez que el United busca entrenador, y mantiene fama de estar abierto a volver a la Premier League. Julian Nagelsmann aparece a cuota 5.5, en tercer lugar. El técnico alemán, destituido de la selección de Alemania tras la decepción en el Mundial, sigue siendo un perfil que seduce al club, y se dice que el responsable de reclutamiento, Christopher Vivell, es uno de sus grandes admiradores. Ofrecería una identidad táctica distinta, aunque su perfil, a medio camino entre la autoridad de Conte y la cercanía de Howe, genera dudas sobre si el United quiere dar un salto tan marcado. Hace una semana, un medio inglés hablaba de una carrera a dos entre él y Howe, un escenario que hoy ha perdido solidez con la entrada de Pochettino. Antonio Conte cotiza a 7. El italiano, que dejó el Napoli un año después de ganar la Serie A, es el candidato más ganador de todos, pero también el que más riesgo implica. Es un técnico que exige, que cambia estructuras y que tiene un historial de fricciones con las directivas. En un club con tantas luchas de poder internas, esa combinación puede resultar explosiva, y los analistas lo consideran una opción poco probable, aunque con un potencial de impacto inmediato que ningún otro candidato iguala. Unai Emery completa la lista, también a cuota 7. El técnico del Aston Villa es, según varias informaciones, la solución soñada de la directiva, y el que mejor encajaría en el perfil que busca el club. El problema es convencerle de dejar un proyecto en el que está cómodo y arrancarlo del Villa sería una operación muy complicada y cara. Por eso, su cuota es la de un candidato que genera ilusión, pero que difícilmente se materialice.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Luke Littler grouped with Beau Greaves as he looks to defend title in Wolverhampton
articles.summary: Luke Littler has been drawn in Group A alongside Beau Greaves and Niels Zonneveld at the Grand Slam of Darts 2026; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
Littler and Greaves have faced each other twice before, with each young star picking up a victory and they will once again face-off in the evening session on Saturday November 14.

The world No 1 and two-time defending champion in Wolverhampton beat Greaves 6-5 in a deciding-leg at Players Championship 24 back in August.

Greaves beat Littler in a 6-5 thriller to clinch a spot in the World Youth Championship final in 2025.

Zonneveld and Littler played each other earlier this year, with the former securing a 6-5 win in the quarter-finals of the European Tour in March. Meanwhile, Greaves beat Zonneveld 6-3 in their meeting in Players Championship 31.

Luke Humphries, the 2023 winner, will take on Joe Cullen and Paolo Nebrida, while Group K catches the eye as James Wade faces Ricky Evans and Cam Crabtree.

Lisa Ashton is in Group B alongside Jermaine Wattimena and Alan Soutar, with Josh Rock in Group C with Kevin Doets and Tommy Morris, who surprisingly won Players Championship 34 recently.

Stephen Bunting, Cameron Menzies, Gerwyn Price, Jonny Clayton, Michael van Gerwen, Chris Dobey, Rob Cross, Gian van Veen, Ross Smith and Nathan Aspinall are also involved in the tournament.

articles.title: Los otros deportistas presidentes: un esgrimista en Hungría, un futbolista en Liberia...
articles.standfirst: Teddy Riner, que quiere ser presidente de Francia, no sería el primer deportista que acaba como jefe de Estado de un país.
articles.summary: Teddy Riner, que quiere ser presidente de Francia, no sería el primer deportista que acaba como jefe de Estado de un país.
articles.body: Teddy Riner quiere ser presidente de la República Francesa. El judoca, pentacampeón olímpico, se presentará a las elecciones presidenciales en 2027. Si saliera elegido, no sería el primer deportista que llega a la jefatura de un Estado a través de las urnas. Ahmed Ben Bella fue el primer presidente de la República Argelina Democrática y Popular después de su independencia en 1962. Ejerció el cargo hasta el golpe de Estado del 19 de junio de 1965. Antes, había jugado al fútbol en Orán para luego militar en el Olympique de Marsella durante la temporada 1939-1940. Sólo disputó un partido de la Copa de Francia, pero marcó uno de los nueve goles en la victoria por 9-1 ante el Antibes. George Weah también saltó del fútbol a la política. El exdelantero del Milan, entre otros equipos, ejerció como presidente de la República de Liberia desde el 22 de enero de 2018 hasta el 22 de enero de 2024. Antes había sido senador. Tras jugar en varios clubes africanos, en 1988 dio el salto a Europa de la mano del Mónaco. Tras cuatro temporadas fichó por el París Saint-Germain. En 1995 llegó a Milan. Luego pasó por el Chelsea, el Manchester City y el Olympique de Marsella antes de retirarse en el Al-Jazira. Míjeil Kavelashvili es actualmente presidente de Georgia. Antes de entrar de lleno en la política en 2016, se labró una buena carrera futbolística. Tras despuntar en el Dinamo Tiflis, fichó por el Manchester City en 1996. Luego su trayectoria se desarrolló en Suiza (Grasshopper, Zúrich, Lucerna, Sion, Aarau y Basilea). Fue 46 veces internacional con Georgia. Pál Schmitt fue presidente de Hungría tras una amplia carrera deportiva en la esgrima. Participó en tres Juegos Olímpicos. Fue oro con el equipo de espada en México 68 y Múnich 72. Fue dos veces campeón del mundo. En 1989 fue nombrado presidente del Comité Olímpico Húngaro, cargo que mantiene a día de hoy. Fue embajador de Hungría en España antes de dedicarse de lleno a la política. El 29 de junio de 2010 fue elegido presidente de Hungría al obtener los votos de 263 diputados. El 2 de abril de 2012 dimitió a raíz de que se conociera que había plagiado su tesis doctoral. Marcus Stephen fue el presidente de la República de Nauru entre 2007 y 2011. Su carrera deportiva arrancó en el fútbol australiano, antes de pasar a la halterofilia, lo que motivó la creación de la Federación de Nauru. En los Juegos de Barcelona 92 participó bajo la bandera de Samoa, ya que su país no tenía Comité Olímpico propio. A partir de los Juegos de Atlanta, ya sí representó a Nauru. En la cita de Sídney portó la antorcha olímpica. Otros jefes de Estado también han tenido un pasado como deportistas presentes en los Juegos Olímpicos. En su caso son o han sido reyes. Entre ellos, están Juan Carlos I (vela en 1972) y Felipe VI (vela en 1992). Alberto de Mónaco fue olímpico en bobsleigh en de 1988 a 2002. Harald de Noruega fue el rey más veces olímpico: tres participaciones en vela de 1964 a 1972 y un diploma olímpico. Su padre Olaf V fue campeón, también en vela, en 1928. Por su parte, el rey Constantino II de Grecia ganó el oro olímpico en vela (clase Dragón) en los Juegos de Roma 1960. Un peldaño por debajo de los jefes de Estado encontramos a primeros ministros o presidentes de Gobierno que también fueron destacados deportistas. Imran Khan ejerció el cargo en Pakistán desde 2018 hasta 2022 (destituido en una moción de censura). Como jugador de críquet, fue capitán de la selección entre 1982 y 1992. En su último año ganó la única Copa del Mundo que brilla en el palmarés de Pakistán. El japonés Taro Aso, primer ministro de 2008 a 2009, fue olímpico en tiro en Montreal.

articles.title: Magnus Ditlev logra la mejor marca de la historia en un IRONMAN
articles.standfirst: El triatleta danés, un gigante de 1,95 metros, gana el IRONMAN Florida en Panama City Beach y bate la plusmarca del noruego y oro olímpico en Tokio Kristian Blummenfelt
articles.summary: El triatleta danés, un gigante de 1,95 metros, gana el IRONMAN Florida en Panama City Beach y arrebata la plusmarca al noruego y oro olímpico en Tokio Kristian Blummenfelt
articles.body: Hace 30 años, el alemán Lothar Leder se convertía en el primer hombre en romper la barrera de las ocho horas en un IRONMAN, la prueba más icónica del triatlón incluso por delante de la olímpica. Ese día en Roth (Alemania), Leder derribaba una barrera que había durado casi 20 años, desde la disputa del primer IRONMAN en la isla de Oahu, Hawaii, en febrero de 1978. La prueba, huelga decir, es una 'salvajada' que combina 3,8 kilómetros a nado, 180 kilómetros en bicicleta y un maratón a pie. Ese primer IRONMAN de la historia lo ganó un estadounidense llamado Gordon Haller en 11 horas, 46 minutos y 58 segundos. Casi medio siglo después, la profesionalización de este deporte ha convertido ese registro e incluso el de Leder en papel mojado. El último ejemplo se vivió el pasado sábado con la disputa del IRONMAN Florida en Panama City Beach, una prueba que encumbró al danés Magnus Ditlev. Ditlev completó todo el recorrido en 7 horas, 19 minutos y 17 segundos, mejorando en casi dos minutos el tiempo (7h21:12) del noruego y oro olímpico en Tokio 2020 Kristian Blummenfelt en el IRONMAN de Cozumel en 2021. Cabe mencionar que en el triatlón no se habla expresamente de récords del mundo por la disparidad de condiciones entre una prueba y otra pero lo que sí se puede decir es que el registro del danés es una 'marcianada' en toda regla. Ditlev llegaba a Florida con una deuda pendiente tras lo ocurrido en el Mundial de la especialidad un mes antes. Ese día en Kona (Hawaii), en la meca del IRONMAN, el danés abandonaba a falta de 10 kilómetros para acabar el maratón cuando lideraba la prueba. "De repente se apagaron las luces", diría luego, en un día caluroso y húmedo que pasó factura a muchos triatletas. El gigante escandinavo (1,95) completó el segmento de natación en 47:52 -salió quinto del agua-, voló sobre la bici (3h51:16) -el mejor tiempo de la historia- y remató con el mejor maratón de su vida (2h33.31), para aventajar en casi 15 minutos (7h33:25) al estadounidense Rudy Von Berg y en dos más a su compatriota Matt Hanson (7h35:48), que remontó de las 18ª plaza al podio en el maratón con el mejor crono en este tramo (2h28:07). "Quizá suene mal decirlo, pero fue el IRONMAN más fácil que he hecho. Sentía el control todo el tiempo", aseguró el danés al valorar con notable modestia su gesta. Ni que decir tiene que Ditlev acabó también radiante tras su récord pero su discurso no cambia y ya piensa en 2027: "Kona era mi mayor objetivo, mi gran oportunidad de ganar allí. Sigo pensando mucho en eso porque lo que me falta es un título mundial".

articles.title: College Football Playoff is expanding to 24 teams in 2027
articles.summary: The College Football Playoff is expanding once again.
articles.body: The College Football Playoff is expanding once again. The CFP will switch to a 24-team format for the 2027 season, the organization announced Monday. The new playoffs will double the number of postseason teams from the current format, the 12-team playoff, which began in 2024. Under the 24-team field, each Power 4 conference champion will receive an automatic bid. There will be 19 at-large bids, and an auto-bid for the highest-ranked Group of 6 school. (The Group of 6 consists of the the American Athletic, Sun Belt, Mid-America, Mountain West, and Pac-12 conferences, as well Conference USA.) The top 25 teams will still be ranked by the CFP selection committee. The Power 4 — which includes the Big Ten, SEC, ACC and Big 12 — will no longer host conference championships under the new rules. Instead, their champions will be determined by regular season standings and conference-determined tiebreakers. In the new format, the top eight teams will receive first-round byes. Teams ranked nine through 16 will host those ranked 17 through 24 at their own stadiums to begin the playoffs, with the second round also taking place on campus, bringing the total number of games played at home stadiums to 16. The quarterfinals and semifinals will still take place at the New Year’s six bowls, the Rose, Fiesta, Sugar, Orange, Peach and Cotton bowls. “The decision to expand was driven by a desire to increase opportunities for FBS programs, student-athletes and fan bases to participate in the Playoff and have a chance to play for the CFP National Championship, while new scheduling standards incentivize institutions to schedule more compelling non-conference matchups during the regular season,” the CFP said in a statement. As a result of the new format, the annual Army-Navy game will be moved to what used to be conference championship week, typically the first Saturday in December. There will be no other games scheduled for that day. The CFP was first introduced in 2014, when only four teams made the postseason. The four-team playoff was in effect through 2023, after which the field tripled to 12 teams. After only three seasons of the 12-team format, the CFP will soon have six times the number of teams than when it first began. No format has been able to avoid controversy so far. In 2023, for example, the last year of the four-team format, an undefeated Florida State team was omitted from the playoff after a late-season injury to its starting quarterback — the first time an undefeated Power 4 school was left out of the postseason. Last year, Notre Dame was left out of the playoff in the committee’s final ranking, falling below Miami after leading the Hurricanes in every ranking until the ultimate one. Next year’s college football regular season will begin the week before Labor Day, on the weekend previously known as Week 0. The regular season will conclude on the final weekend of November. The 24-team format will be in place for at least five seasons, beginning next year through the 2031-32 season.

articles.title: Así están las cuentas: ¿Qué necesita cada equipo para clasificar a los cuadrangulares de la Liga BetPlay?
articles.standfirst: Seis equipos, tres cupos y todo por definir: las cuentas fatales para entrar a los cuadrangulares
articles.summary: Seis equipos, tres cupos y todo por definir: las cuentas fatales para entrar a los cuadrangulares
articles.body: La fase regular de la Liga BetPlay 2026-II entra en su recta definitiva y el rentado nacional vive horas de máxima tensión. Con varios equipos ya instalados en la siguiente instancia, la atención se concentra en la parte media-alta de la tabla, donde seis clubes pelean de forma directa por los últimos tres cupos disponibles a los cuadrangulares semifinales. La calculadora y las matemáticas son las principales protagonistas de esta jornada de cierre. A continuación, analizamos en detalle cómo está la tabla de posiciones y qué necesita cada uno de los implicados para meterse en la pelea por el título del fútbol colombiano. Hasta el momento, históricos como Atlético Nacional, América de Cali, Deportivo Cali, Atlético Bucaramanga e Independiente Santa Fe ya aseguraron su tiquete anticipado. Por su parte, el grupo de los seis equipos que se disputan los tres cupos restantes lo conforman: Independiente Medellín (29 puntos, +3) Millonarios (27 puntos, +9) Once Caldas (27 puntos, +4) Deportes Tolima (26 puntos, +2) Águilas Doradas (25 puntos, +1) Cúcuta Deportivo (24 puntos, -5) Cada escuadra maneja un escenario diferente de cara a la última fecha de la Liga BetPlay. Estos son los detalles y las combinaciones que necesitan: 1. Independiente Medellín (29 puntos | Diferencia: +3) El panorama: Es el club mejor ubicado y con la situación más favorable del grupo de aspirantes. Qué necesita: Enfrentará a Águilas Doradas. Un empate le basta para asegurar su cupo a los cuadrangulares, llegando a 30 unidades y superando en los ítems de desempate a varios rivales. Incluso perdiendo podría clasificar si no se dan triunfos combinados de Millonarios, Once Caldas, Tolima y Cúcuta. 2. Millonarios (27 puntos | Diferencia: +9) El panorama: Los embajadores cerrarán la fase regular jugando como locales en el estadio El Campín frente a Alianza FC. Qué necesita: Una victoria sella su clasificación de manera directa. Si empata, tendrá que esperar que Once Caldas o Deportes Tolima no ganen sus respectivos encuentros, además de vigilar que el Cúcuta Deportivo no arrebate plazas con puntaje perfecto. 3. Once Caldas (27 puntos | Diferencia: +4) El panorama: El 'Blanco Blanco' depende de sí mismo en una plaza siempre compleja: visitará a Atlético Nacional en el estadio Atanasio Girardot. Qué necesita: Ganar lo clasificará automáticamente sin mirar otros resultados. Un empate le sirve siempre y cuando el Tolima no gane, Águilas no golea al DIM o el Cúcuta no sume la totalidad de los puntos pendientes. Una derrota por marcador amplio lo dejaría altamente expuesto a la diferencia de gol. 4. Deportes Tolima (26 puntos | Diferencia: +2) El panorama: El 'Pijao' está obligado a remar contra corriente en la última fecha y visitará al Deportivo Cali en el estadio de Palmaseca. Qué necesita: La consigna es ganar o ganar y esperar tropiezos de Independiente Medellín, Millonarios u Once Caldas. Si empata, necesita que el Once Caldas pierda por una diferencia de dos o más goles, y que ni Águilas ni Cúcuta superen la línea de los 27 puntos. 5. Águilas Doradas (25 puntos | Diferencia: +1) El panorama: Con 25 unidades, el margen de error del conjunto dorado es mínimo y se jugará la vida visitando a Independiente Medellín. Qué necesita: Únicamente le sirve la victoria ante el DIM, sumada a una combinación de resultados que incluya derrotas o empates de Millonarios u Once Caldas, que el Tolima no sume de a tres y que el Cúcuta no logre puntaje perfecto. Cualquier otro resultado lo dejaría virtualmente eliminado. 6. Cúcuta Deportivo (24 puntos | Diferencia: -5) El panorama: Es el equipo más comprometido de los seis por dos factores: el puntaje y su diferencia de gol negativa (-5), siendo el único de este lote con ese apartado en contra. Qué necesita: Está obligado a ganar sus partidos pendientes (necesita sumar los 6 puntos en disputa para llegar a 30) y aguardar combinaciones milagrosas, como caídas de Millonarios u Once Caldas, o tropiezos del Medellín. Si cede puntos en cualquiera de sus salidas, quedará sentenciado a la eliminación. La Dimayor anunciará en las próximas horas la programación oficial de la jornada 19, una fecha que paralizará al país futbolero con partidos en simultáneo donde cada gol cambiará drásticamente la tabla de posiciones en vivo.

articles.title: El Bayern Múnich ya tiene en la mira al reemplazo de Luis Díaz: la joya por la que pagaría una millonaria cláusula
articles.standfirst: Bayern Múnich pone la mira en Oskar Pietuszewski: el heredero que busca para Luis Díaz
articles.summary: Bayern Múnich pone la mira en Oskar Pietuszewski: el heredero que busca para Luis Díaz
articles.body: El Bayern Múnich ya piensa en el futuro a largo plazo de su plantilla y ha puesto el radar en una de las jóvenes sensaciones del fútbol europeo. Ante la necesidad de blindar su banda izquierda y encontrar un socio y eventual relevo de garantías para el colombiano Luis Díaz, la dirección deportiva del gigante bávaro ha comenzado a seguir de cerca los pasos del joven extremo polaco Oskar Pietuszewski. Con apenas 18 años, Pietuszewski se ha convertido en uno de los nombres propios del mercado internacional. El atacante, que destaca por su desborde, velocidad y capacidad asociativa en el uno contra uno, ha llamado la atención de los principales ojeadores de Europa gracias a su proyección en el extremo izquierdo. Para el técnico del Bayern, Vincent Kompany, contar con alternativas de élite en los costados es una prioridad absoluta. Si bien el estratega belga ha tenido que improvisar en ocasiones utilizando a futbolistas como Alphonso Davies en posiciones más adelantadas debido a problemas físicos en la plantilla, la directiva busca una solución de perfil natural y de proyección generacional. La lesión sufrida por Luis Díaz en el tramo reciente de la temporada dejó en evidencia la dependencia del equipo muniqués en el extremo izquierdo. Aunque el extremo de la Selección Colombia continúa siendo una pieza fundamental e indiscutible en el esquema titular de los bávaros, la gerencia deportiva liderada por la cúpula del Allianz Arena entiende que es vital estructurar una plantilla profunda que mantenga el nivel competitivo ante cualquier contratiempo físico. En este escenario, la incorporación de un perfil joven como el de Pietuszewski encajaría perfectamente en la política de fichajes del club: apostar por talento emergente que pueda foguearse bajo la tutela de figuras mundiales antes de asumir galones de estelaridad. A pesar del fuerte interés del Bayern Múnich, fichar a la joven promesa no será una tarea sencilla ni económica: Los próximos meses serán cruciales para determinar si el Bayern Múnich decide dar el paso definitivo en el mercado de fichajes de verano e iniciar negociaciones formales para asegurar a una de las joyas llamadas a dominar el continente europeo en la próxima década.

articles.title: Rachel Maddow says trans sports debate is a made up issue to harm trans people
articles.summary: Rachel Maddow calls the trans athletes debate a "fantasy" and "repulsive," but 2026 midterm results and national polling tell a very different story.
articles.body: MS Now host Rachel Maddow says the trans sports debate is a made-up issue. She claims those pushing it are participating in a "repulsive" political campaign. Maddow discussed the topic this week on the "Pablo Torre Finds Out" podcast. "It turns out the trans athletes thing, I mean, there are a lot of actual, very serious elements of it. No. 1 is just seeing this national, insistent, now years-long political project to scapegoat and vilify and try to direct violence and hate toward a tiny, disfavored minority, which is trans people," Maddow began. CARTON RIPS INTO PHILADELPHIA EAGLES HEAD COACH NICK SIRIANNI, SAYS HE COACHED HIS EVER GAME IN PHILADELPHIA - LISTEN NOW "That is something that has a profound, profound impact on some of our fellow Americans. And it is repulsive. It is politically as transparent as any other exercise like this has been from any other authoritarian movement in politics, in any country, in the last century and a half." She then declared the issue a "fantasy." "And politically, it is a fantasy to invent a fake problem, to invent something that has literally no contact with the real lives of 99.9999% of Americans and say this is the problem that the American government must be reorganized to prioritize and to never solve for you, so we can continue to run on it forever. "It is pitiful, a sign of profound political weakness, and something that I think has now been exposed as the fantasist BS copout that it is." Voters disagree, including Democratic voters. During the 2026 midterms, left-leaning Washington state and Colorado approved measures requiring transgender athletes to compete in school sports categories that match their sex. National polling from Gallup found that around 78% of voters oppose allowing men who identify as women to compete in female athletics. The Democrats currently have some winning messages on their side. The results of the midterm prove that, particularly amid concerns about the ongoing war in Iran and everyday costs in America. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE However, defending males competing in female sports is not one of them. No honest person argues that keeping males out of female athletics is voters' greatest concern. It isn't. Fuel prices, grocery costs, and housing affect far more Americans directly. But voters do care. In September, polling from The 19th/YouGov found that around half of voters favor candidates who support trans sports bans. Many respondents worried that ignoring the issue would allow it to become more common. Some voters prioritize the issue because they want to prevent it from affecting them or their children. That is what Maddow misses when she claims trans sports has "no contact with the real lives of 99.9999% of Americans." Parents do not have to wait until their daughters lose a roster spot or share a locker room with a male to object. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Further, there's something eerie about adults like Maddow telling young girls they need not worry about competing against males in female athletics. Perhaps telling girls to "shut up and change next to this biological male" is what is, to use Maddow's term, repulsive.

For as bad as the Colts offense has been lately, they still have one of the 10-best fantasy RB schedules in the second half of the season, so McGowan could be a sneaky fantasy RB3 down the stretch.

The elite backup RBs who are one-injury away from stardom should be rostered everywhere and I'll continue to highlight them in this space until they no longer qualify for this article.

It was clear early in the season that Johnson was one of the best backups to roster, in case anything ever happens to Kenneth Walker III. In recent weeks, Johnson's value has increased even more now that he's offering weekly flex production.

The rookie posted a fluky 128 receiving yards and a score in Week 8, but he followed it up with 34 yards and another touchdown on Sunday. Upcoming matchups with the Falcons, Cardinals and Bills are all spots where Johnson could be a viable flex play while also offering league-winning upside if Walker ever misses time.

Black is in the same situation as Johnson, you can basically just swap Walker's name with Christian McCaffrey's in the previous section.

The 49ers' rookie plays in one of the best offenses in the league and has flashed his potential with at least 60 rushing yards in three of his first eight games, while serving as CMC's direct backup. That includes the past two games, when Black turned 12 touches into 63 yards and a TD against the Falcons, as well as Sunday's outing, which resulted in 11 carries for a season-high 70 yards.

Next up is the Cowboys defense that's a top-five matchup for fantasy running backs. The 49ers are 4-point favorites in a game with the highest projected point total in Week 10 at 55.5.

Stashing a talented No. 2 back playing behind a 30-year-old starter who handled 450 touches last year is just an obvious move. Black should be rostered everywhere as a flex option with RB1 upside if McCaffrey were ever sidelined.

Rhamondre Stevenson left Sunday's game with a knee injury and was very quickly ruled out. Mike Vrabel didn't have an update Monday morning, but did acknowledge that his back was undergoing an MRI. With TreVeyon Henderson already sidelined indefinitely, that leaves Kiner as the next man up.

Though Kiner hasn't been asked to do much as a pass-catcher, the 2025 UDFA has shown some juice in the run game by topping 50 yards in three of his last five outings in a change-of-pace role.

If Stevenson can't suit up in Week 10, Kiner immediately becomes a high-end fantasy RB3 with the usual touchdown upside that comes with a starter. We can't lock that outcome in though until we get a proper update on Stevenson's injury.

Josh Jacobs fractured his finger and is set to undergo surgery that will keep him out a maximum of three games.

MarShawn Lloyd missed Week 9 due to a knee injury, which allowed Johnson to step up in Jacobs' absence. Johnson finished with 68 yards and a touchdown, making him the RB11 on the week with just MNF left to be played.

If you're wondering why Johnson isn't higher on this list, just take a look at Green Bay's upcoming schedule. The Packers face the Vikings this week, then have a bye before taking on the Rams.

So, even with Jacobs sidelined, this isn't the ideal setup for a spot starter. On top of that, we aren't sure if/when Lloyd will be available. If Lloyd is active in Week 10, it only further muddies the projections.

If Lloyd remains out, Johnson would be a risky RB3/flex versus the Vikings. If Lloyd plays, then both players would be risky flex options.

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

DeMario Douglas has always been a risky receiver to put in your fantasy lineup due to his low floor. We witnessed that occur in Week 7, when he only delivered three catches for 23 yards.

However, Douglas has posted at least 12 fantasy points in his other four outings over the last five weeks, finishing as a top-10 WR three times. After hauling in five of his nine targets for 102 yards in Week 9, he currently sits as the WR23 with just Monday Night Football remaining.

Four touchdowns during this stretch have helped his cause, but he's come away with very respectable yardage totals in these games with at least 65 in each.

A.J. Brown's recovery timeline remains uncertain and with a bye looming, it seems likely we won't see him until Week 12 at the earliest. Fantasy managers can continue to take advantage by starting Douglas as a WR3/flex option with temporary upside.

Douglas has played four games this year that weren't impacted by injury. In those contests, the rookie has posted stat lines of 5-94-0, 2-70-2, 4-43-0 and 6-70-0.

With Malik Willis nursing a groin injury that's limited him as a runner, Douglas has seen 14 targets over the past two weeks.

When a first-year player is showing this kind of production early in his career, it's worth taking notice. Douglas can be started as a WR3/flex, especially given his intriguing matchups against the Colts and Bills the next two weeks.

After back-to-back games with at least 50 yards, it was discouraging to see Williams underwhelm with just three catches for 25 yards this week. I'm still holding out hope though.

The rookie continues to play the most snaps and run the most routes in the Commanders' receiver room. This was the third straight outing where Williams accomplished that feat, following Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury.

It's possible Williams levels off as a low-ceiling WR4/flex option for fantasy, but I'm holding for at least another week. The talent is evident and Washington has one of the top-10 easiest schedules for fantasy receivers the rest of the way.

It's easy to forget, but Bryant had a growing role in the Broncos' passing attack during the opening month before being placed on injured reserve with an ankle injury. In those first four games, Bryant topped 40 yards three times.

So, it was great to see him post a season-high 56 yards and a touchdown on four catches in his first game back since the injury. Jaylen Waddle also suffered a concussion, but he should be cleared after their Week 10 bye.

Regardless, Bryant was a borderline flex option early in the season and has returned with an even better performance. Given Waddle's struggles and Courtland Sutton's age, there's a non-zero chance Bryant becomes the most valuable fantasy receiver in Denver for the rest of the season.

Watkins' fantasy value is difficult to assess because it's entirely dependent on the health of the other receivers in San Francisco.

Deebo Samuel Sr. is nearing a return from a hamstring injury that kept him out for the last month. Mike Evans' Achilles tendinitis is an ongoing problem with no clear recovery timeline. I'll be surprised if he suits up in Week 10. Demarcus Robinson is apparently playing at less than 100%, while De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk are on IR.

That opened the door for Watkins, who put up four receptions, 86 yards and a touchdown versus the Raiders. That's his second consecutive quality stat line, after a 56-yard performance versus the Falcons prior to the Niners' Week 8 bye.

If everything remains the same with Evans and Deebo sitting out, Watkins will be a very enticing WR4/flex option in a good matchup with the Cowboys this week.

In the four games since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has posted stat lines for 4-60-0, 7-69-0, 2-32-0 and 6-57-0.

While he hasn't found the end zone, that type of volume (at least six targets in three of the four appearances) makes him the 10th-most targeted tight end on a per game basis during that stretch.

Okonkwo has moved into the high-end TE2 streamer conversation, with a chance to crack the low-end TE1 range moving forward.

Higbee has disappeared from fantasy relevance following his impressive three-game stretch from Week 3 to Week 5, when he posted 8-62-1, 5-67-0 and 5-83-0. Since then, the veteran has been held to 22 yards or less in four straight contests and hasn't found the end zone.

It's possible MHJ could carve out a bigger role as the season progresses, but it's highly unlikely he'll make a major fantasy impact — unless Collins gets hurt. articles.title: Catching Strays | Knicks’ Andre Drummond is outrebounding Mitchell Robinson
articles.summary: This is Catching Strays, the Daily News’ regular Knicks rundown for the quotes, stats and storylines that didn’t make a headline. Today: Early returns on And...
articles.body:
This is Catching Strays, the Daily News' regular Knicks rundown for the quotes, stats and storylines that didn't make a headline.

Today: Early returns on Andre Drummond and Mitchell Robinson, Giannis Antetokounmpo responds to Doc Rivers' criticism, and where the Knicks rank on leaguewide leaderboards.

More boards. Fewer minutes. Better from the line.

The Knicks signed Andre Drummond to replace Mitchell Robinson, who left for the Boston Celtics as a free agent in the offseason. The idea was never that Drummond would be Robinson. It was that he would take the open job: the backup minutes behind Karl-Anthony Towns on a team attempting to repeat as NBA champions.

Nine games in, both sides of that comparison are on the table.

Drummond has come off the bench in all nine games. He is averaging 7.8 rebounds (three coming on the offensive glass) and five points in 13.3 minutes a night. Robinson has played nine games, too, but he began the season as a starter and has since taken on a role as backup to Celtics big man Neemias Queta. The ex-Knicks defensive anchor is averaging 6.4 points and 5.7 rebounds through his first nine games in Boston.

The difference in rebounding is even wider when factoring in that Robinson has played considerably more minutes than Drummond. Per 36 minutes, Drummond is averaging a towering 21 rebounds (the highest rate of his career), while Robinson sits at 10.9 per 36, marking a decline for him.

On top of that, Drummond is shooting 58% from the free throw line. Robinson has made a third of his attempts from the charity stripe this season. Drummond ranks second behind San Antonio's Tarris Reed Jr. in rebounds per 36 minutes (21). Robinson ranks 65th (10.1).

The last three games each actually played make the same point in a tighter window. Drummond has 26 rebounds in just under 40 minutes: nine in 13 minutes against Brooklyn, nine in 12 minutes against Chicago and eight in 14 minutes at Cleveland. Robinson has 24 rebounds over his last three games, but he played 53 minutes to get them. His last win came Sunday night in Milwaukee, when he finished with 12 points, seven rebounds (four offensive), four steals, two assists and a block in 18 minutes.

Nine games is still an early look. It is enough to put the two lines next to each other and see what the job looks like so far. Drummond is not Robinson. He is playing Mitch's minutes, however, and he is getting more rebounds in fewer of them.

Giannis speechless after Doc — then Christie piles on

Giannis Antetokounmpo was visibly frustrated when presented with comments made by his former Milwaukee Bucks head coach Doc Rivers, who questioned the two-time league MVP's basketball IQ in an episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast on Nov. 5.

"Oh my God, first of all, he's not my coach," Antetokounmpo said on Sunday. "My coach is coach [Erik Spoelstra], but he's a coach that I've worked with in the past. I'm speechless.

"You got to go ask him why he thought that. That's on him, that's not on me. I just got to focus on my team and what I got to do and how I can be better and how I can help the team. But that's crazy. Never let bitterness or pettiness get in front of your goals and dreams, man. For every athlete out there, never let that. That's insane. But you got to go ask him why he said what he said, not me."

Rivers, who is now an analyst for NBC, framed last season's exit as a dance neither side wanted to own. The Bucks eventually traded Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat for a package headlined by Tyler Herro, young players and draft compensation.

"Giannis wanted out, but he was a Buck. And he didn't want to be the bad guy," Rivers said on the Nov. 5 episode. "He wanted [management] and those guys to say, 'We're trading you,' instead of him asking for a trade. To me, that was the game that was being played.

"I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude," Rivers continued. "He's interesting. He's not easy. … He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time. … He really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

Antetokounmpo's response came after Miami's 114-108 win in Sacramento. The same night, Kings head coach Doug Christie was asked about the shot profile that let Antetokounmpo cook from midrange for 29 points and 14 rebounds. Christie was living with contested midrange looks — until they went in.

"You know, even the shot profile was Giannis shooting a mid-range, contested shot. We're living with that. Tonight, he knocked them down," Christie said. "I'll watch him next game, he probably won't."

Separately, Bill Simmons — on a later Bill Simmons Podcast segment circulating Monday — said the Celtics made the right call in the summer trade chase.

"Honestly, they made the right move with Giannis," Simmons said. "I don't think they wanted him. I saw him in person on Wednesday. I talked about him with Doc on Thursday, which started a two-day news cycle. But he [Giannis] is not the same guy that he was five years ago."

Shamet's threes are holding while he fills in for Hart

Landry Shamet has played all nine games and is 20-of-48 (.417) from three. He has started two — Nov. 4 against Chicago and Nov. 7 at Cleveland — with Josh Hart out both nights with right ankle soreness. That is nine games of volume and a percentage that has held while the starter minutes moved, but not a claim on a qualified league leaderboard.

The leaderboards that do count have other Knicks on them.

Karl-Anthony Towns is first in the league in double-doubles: nine in nine games, all points and rebounds. Giannis is next at eight, then Domantas Sabonis and Victor Wembanyama at seven. Towns also ranks second in rebounds at 13.6 a night, first in defensive rebounds at 10.2 (92 total), eighth in offensive rebounds at 3.3 and third in total rebounds at 122.

Jalen Brunson is ninth in scoring at 26.2 points a night. Andre Drummond is tied for 10th in offensive rebounds at three. Hart, in seven games, is seventh in steals at 2.1.

Tyler Kolek's number is the assist-to-turnover rate: nine-to-one — 36 assists and 4 turnovers in 87 minutes over seven games. Kolek is first in assists per 36 minutes (14.9) and assists per 100 possessions (20.7).
authors: Kristian Winfield, New York Daily News

articles.title: Will Paul Toboni and the Washington Nationals make any noise at the GM Meetings?
articles.summary: The GM meetings are not usually the most explosive part of the offseason but that could change with the lockout looming
articles.body:
Today is actually the first day of the GM Meetings in Las Vegas. Most years, the GM meetings don't result in any massive moves, instead they set the scene for things that happen later in the offseason. However, this year could be different due to the looming lockout. Teams could be more active this year, and the Nats could take advantage of that.

Jon Morosi reported that trade discussions are more advanced than they usually are at this point of the offseason. This is almost certainly due to the fact that teams will not be able to make roster moves when the lockout begins in early December. There is a real deadline in place, so that means GM's will be working with more urgency.

We may only see one or two deals during the meetings themselves, which run from November 9th to the 12th. However, I would not be surprised if we see things really pick up in the next week or so. If the last labor dispute is any indicator, a lot of the top free agents will fly off the board in the end of November.

In the 2021 offseason, Corey Seager, Marcus Semien, Max Scherzer and Javier Baez were among the names to sign contracts worth over $100 million before the lockout started. This offseason, we could see players such as Tarik Skubal, Randy Arozarena and Seiya Suzuki sign mega-deals.

Mark Feinsand of MLB.com wrote a good breakdown of what we should expect from the GM Meetings. It is a good time for the new executives to get themselves acquainted and for the groundwork of deals to be laid. Executives will be doing a lot of chatting, and surely some interesting trade proposals will be exchanged.

I wonder what this could mean for CJ Abrams. If the Nats were to pull the trigger on an Abrams trade, it would make the most sense to do it before the lockout. GM's will certainly be calling or chatting with Paul Toboni and the Nats brass about Abrams. To be honest, I do not have a great feel on whether the Nats will make the move this offseason.

When last offseason came around, I was fairly confident that MacKenzie Gore would be dealt and Abrams would stay. While I wanted the Nats to be a player in free agency, my hopes were not high. This offseason, I am less sure about what they will do.

After making big strides during the 2026 season, things are less cut and dry for Paul Toboni. This is not a full scale rebuild anymore. The Nats are not contenders yet, but they also should not be trading big pieces just for the sake of it.

During the GM Meetings and the week following the event, I think we will get more clarity about what Paul Toboni's plans are. He has already shown he is not afraid to act and make big moves. These next few weeks could be huge in determining what the next few years of Nats baseball looks like. The groundwork for these actions will be laid out at the GM Meetings this week in Vegas.

articles.title: Dodgers Face Threat to Alex Vesia Reunion as Marlins Enter Picture
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers are already facing competition for one of their top free agents, Alex Vesia.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are already facing competition for one of their top free agents, Alex Vesia.

According to Kevin Barral of Fish on First , the Marlins are targeting Alex Vesia as a free agent as they hope to upgrade their bullpen, specifically looking for a lefty.

Along with Vesia, San Diego Padres free agent Adrian Morejon and Chicago White Sox southpaw Sean Newcomb are two other options.

The Marlins have a ton of right-handed options on their staff, but they lack southpaw options, and they could end up bringing in a couple of lefties.

Vesia has been one of the steadiest relievers in baseball, with few dips in form, especially over the last three years.

He has a stellar 2.45 ERA over the last three seasons and 4.3 bWAR, avoiding any kind of major injuries and pitching 184 innings over that time frame.

His fastball velocity has declined over the last few years, but his funky arm slot and outlier fastball movement mean he can overcome any loss of steam.

Free agents can be volatile, given how inconsistent bullpen pitching can be and how reliant some pitchers are on velocity, but Vesia is a sure thing that appeals to contenders and rebuilding teams alike.

The Marlins lie somewhere in the middle, not outright bad, but also lacking the top-end players and production to really make a push.

However, adding a stabilizing force like Vesia raises a team's floor, and it can help add meaningful wins to a team that needs them.

The issue that teams like the Marlins have is that bullpen arms are so valuable, and Vesia is already valued at eight figures per year.

The Dodgers can afford to keep a player who has done so much for the franchise and is projected to continue providing that kind of value.

LA seems to be letting Vesia's market play out, then possibly striking a deal that rewards their long-time contributor.

articles.title: FSU basketball's Luke Loucks shares thoughts on new AD Jeff Purinton
articles.summary: FSU basketball coach Luke Loucks says he is excited to work with new athletic director Jeff Purinton.
articles.body:
Florida State men's basketball head coach Luke Loucks and new athletic director Jeff Purinton may be new to each other, but the pair share a close circle.

Purinton, who was announced as FSU's next athletic director on Monday, Nov. 9 , hired Brian Hodgson (now Providence head coach) and Ryan Pannone, the current Red Wolves head coach and friend of Loucks, during his time at Arkansas State.

Loucks said he spoke with Hodgson and Pannone about Purinton and that he's excited to have someone familiar with FSU coming into the role.

"Talked to both those guys this morning. We have some overlap. Our [sport] oversight, Doug Walker, worked with Jeff at Alabama. So there are a lot of ties, mutual friendships between myself and Jeff," Loucks said after a practice on Monday. Nov. 9. "And all great things. Obviously, to have a Florida State guy, he understands what we're trying to do here."

FAMU basketball battles Florida State in Orion180 Tip-Off Classic

While much of the focus of Purinton's hire has been on the Seminoles football program, men's basketball is a revenue generator in the modern era of collegiate athletics, and Purinton is no stranger to success on the hardwood.

He helped Nate Oats build the Alabama program into a national title contender, and both Hodgson and now Pannone have done well at Arkansas State. Another aspect of Purinton's hire that Loucks said was beneficial is Purinton's understanding of the modern NIL landscape.

While at Learfield, Purinton oversaw NIL, revenue, and multimedia relationships with SEC programs, something Loucks thinks will benefit the university.

"Probably the most important thing in this era is where he's coming from in Learfield. With the NIL, especially with the SEC, that to me just does it better than everyone else in terms of the finances of today's college teams. It sounds like Jeff has a really good grasp of not only how to operate, but how to get ahead in those areas," Loucks said.

"So for all those reasons, I'm really excited to get to know him and his family."

articles.title: LPGA veteran Ryann O’Toole picks up $1 million bonus while awaiting birth of first child
articles.summary: The first bundle of joy for Ryann O’Toole arrived Monday: a $1 million bonus for winning the Aon Risk Reward Challenge for the LPGA Tour season that ended in...
articles.body:
DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. — The first bundle of joy for Ryann O'Toole arrived Monday: a $1 million bonus for winning the Aon Risk Reward Challenge for the LPGA Tour season that ended in September for O'Toole because she is pregnant with her first child.

O'Toole is expecting in January. She played her final event at the FM Championship in August, giving her enough rounds to qualify for the bonus program built around a player's average score on a designated risk-reward hole — typically a par 5 — at each tournament.

With two tournaments left in the challenge, no one can catch her.

The $1 million bonus should come in handy for the 39-year-old O'Toole, who has one career LPGA win and whose most lucrative season was in 2024 when she won just over $629,000. Her career earnings from a 15-year career are $4,706,355.

"A year after going back to Q-Series to earn her card, Ryann finished on top while playing a limited schedule, all while navigating her pregnancy and supporting her brother in his recovery from a severe accident. That's really special golf," LPGA Commissioner Craig Kessler said.

O'Toole improved her ranking in par-5 scoring from 125th on the LPGA in 2025 to 11th this year, helped by a career-best 270.6 average in driving distance.

"Ryann's performance shows what better decision making looks like: understanding the risk, recognizing the opportunity and having the confidence to act when it matters most," said Anne Corona, Aon's CEO of North America. "We are proud to celebrate her as the newest Aon Risk Reward Challenge champion, and we wish Ryann and her partner, Gina, all the best as they prepare to welcome their first child."

Sakuma, an eight-time winner on the LPGA of Japan Tour, finished at 20 under to find the winner's circle for the first time on the LPGA Tour.

articles.title: Clemson star earns ACC award after shutting down Syracuse WR
articles.summary: Ashton Hampton held Syracuse star Umari Hatcher to two catches, grabbed a red-zone interception and earned his first ACC weekly honor.
articles.body:
Dabo Swinney spent last week calling Syracuse receiver Umari Hatcher a "Waldo-type guy" because the Orange moved him all over the field. Clemson's first job before every snap was finding him. Ashton Hampton watched him like a hawk, followed him all night, and like Jafar in Aladdin, made Hatcher disappear.

Hatcher entered Saturday ranked fourth nationally with 119 receiving yards per game. Steve Angeli targeted him nine times against Clemson , but Hatcher finished with season lows of two receptions and 12 yards. That is 107 yards below his average entering the afternoon.

Clemson kept Hampton or Elliot Washington II attached to Hatcher for most of the game. Hampton walked away with eight solo tackles, two pass breakups, and the play that protected Clemson's lead when Syracuse finally threatened to break through.

The Orange reached Clemson's 3-yard line during the fourth quarter with a chance to turn an 18-6 game into a one-possession fight. Jahiem Lawson hit Angeli as he released the ball, forcing it to float into the end zone. Hampton was waiting underneath it for his second interception of the season and the fifth of his Clemson career.

The ACC rewarded him Monday with the first Defensive Back of the Week honor of his career. Hampton joined Washington and safety Jerome Carter III as Clemson defensive backs to win the award this season. It marks the first time since 2000 that three Tigers have earned the honor in the same year.

The Jim Thorpe Award semifinalist now has 14 passes defended, which ranks second nationally and first among power-conference players. He is also one of five players in the country with at least four games containing multiple pass breakups.

articles.title: Notre Dame’s former standout TE gets touchdown for Panthers
articles.summary: It's been a couple of weeks ago since former Notre Dame tight end Tommy Tremble has had a touchdown. That changed when he recorded 1 for the Panthers.
articles.body:
Ex-Notre Dame tight end Tommy Tremble hasn't had a touchdown in a couple of games for the Carolina Panthers .

That changed on Sunday when Tremble hauled in a 10-yard pass from Bryce Young for the score . It was Tremble's first TD since he had two in Carolina's 25-14 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Oct. 18.

See the best photos from Notre Dame's 31-24 win over Miami (FL)

Tremble's TD came in the second quarter when Carolina cut the deficit to 10-7 against the Denver Broncos. The Panthers went on to lose 26-21.

The former Fighting Irish standout finished with four catches for 24-yards on Sunday. Through eight games, Tremble has 21-receptions for 179-yards and three scores for Carolina.

The Denver Broncos have had their share of one-score games recently, and the most recent win got a helping hand from an unexpected source . After the game, Sean Payton mistakenly called out a reporter for smoking in a lighthearted press conference moment, according to a post on X by Zac Stevens.

"Can we not smoke in here?" Payton asked with a stern look on his face. "Please. Oh, you're not smoking. You got a pencil. I'm sorry. I thought you were smoking."

After laughter, Payton added, "I had a flashback, thinking, 'Who's smoking a cigarette?' I'm sorry. I'll start again."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Broncos held off the Panthers for their fifth straight win. It was a tough 26-21 decision at Carolina.

Will the Broncos be a trade deadline player?

While Payton seeks out press conference smokers, the organization may have a deal on its mind to improve the roster for the second half of the season, according to Sports Illustrated.

"I mean, that's impossible to predict," Payton said. "We'll discuss what's out there, and I think we'll see what happens, but I like this team. There's room for us to get better, but I like this team a lot. We just got to take advantage of the position we're sitting in right now."

It's definitely a position of strength for the Broncos. They stand at 7-2 and are No. 5 in the NFL power rankings, according to Fox Sports.

"Head coach Sean Payton is quietly fixing the Broncos' offensive woes while pushing the defense to maintain its dominance," Bucky Brooks wrote. "Although the box score doesn't fully reflect his impact, the Super Bowl-winning coach is pushing the right buttons to inch his squad closer to a top seed in the tournament.

"With 16 one-score wins (eight points or fewer) since the start of last season, the Broncos are built to thrive in the playoffs, which is when tactics and toughness matter more than talent."

Also, the Broncos have a very favorable schedule down the stretch. They get the Raiders twice, the Dolphins, Jets, and Chargers, along with a few tougher games like the Bills.

articles.title: Browns’ Todd Monken not ready to choose between Shedeur Sanders, Deshaun Watson for Week 10
articles.summary: On Sunday afternoon, the Cleveland Browns fell to 5-4 on the season with a tough road loss at the hands of the New Orleans Saints. Shedeur Sanders got the st...
articles.body:
On Sunday afternoon, the Cleveland Browns fell to 5-4 on the season with a tough road loss at the hands of the New Orleans Saints. Shedeur Sanders got the start at quarterback for Cleveland in this one, taking over for Deshaun Watson, who had been in the concussion protocol for most of the week prior to the game.

Recently, Browns head coach Todd Monken was asked about whether there is a chance that Sanders might take over as the full-time starter in Cleveland.

"#Browns Todd Monken said he's not ready to name his starting quarterback for Sunday's game vs. the #Texans," reported Mary Kay Cabot of Cleveland.com on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Sanders had a bit of a shaky start on Sunday against the Saints but showed impressive poise in leading the Browns on a late drive to get the game into overtime, and then leading them down the field once again in the extra period to score a touchdown. Unfortunately, Cleveland's two-point conversion try came up empty, giving the Saints their third win of the season.

In many ways, Sanders' performance echoed what fans have seen out of Watson this year, consistently putting together below-average performances for the majority of the game before turning up the heat late and leading the Browns to several crunch-time wins so far this year.

It will be fascinating to see if what Sanders did on Sunday against the Saints will be enough for Monken to trust him moving forward with the offense, or whether the head coach will hand the keys back to Watson now that he is healthy.

articles.title: Grand Rapids Catholic Central removed from playoffs 1 day before game
articles.summary: Following a brief legal back-and-forth with the MHSAA, Grand Rapids Catholic Central football has been removed from the state playoffs.
articles.body:
The courts have decided that Grand Rapids Catholic Central is out of the Michigan high school football playoffs after all.

A Kent County judge ruled in favor of the Michigan High School Athletic Association in the case of a temporary restraining order for Grand Rapids Catholic Central football, which briefly reinstated the Cougars in the state playoffs. The decision follows a show-cause hearing for the injunction granted to a GRCC student, according to the state high school sports governing body.

The TRO briefly forced the Michigan High School Athletic Association to reinstate Grand Rapids Catholic Central into the state playoffs.

On Thursday, Oct. 29, the MHSAA announced it was removing Grand Rapids Catholic Central from the Division 5 state football playoffs for using an ineligible player. According to the MHSAA, GRCC used an ineligible player for six regular season games, forcing the Cougars to forfeit five wins. The forfeits would drop GRCC to 2-7 and leave it without the playoff points needed to qualify as a top-32 team in Division 5.

The show-cause hearing was on Friday, Nov. 6, with the court issuing its decision on Monday, Nov. 9. It came one day before Grand Rapids Catholic Central was scheduled to face Berrien Springs in the state's last district final.

Berrien Springs wins by forfeit, advancing to play Grand Rapids West Catholic in a Division 5 regional final on Saturday at 1 p.m.

"The MHSAA is thankful for the Court's prompt decision today, confirming the integrity of the MHSAA's eligibility rules, which all of our member schools expect to be enforced as written," the MHSAA said in a statement on Monday, Nov. 9. "As a result of the Court's decision, there will not be a District game played on Tuesday, November 10 th , and Berrien Springs High School will advance to the next round of the playoffs to face Grand Rapids West Catholic High School on Saturday, November 14 at 1 p.m."

In response to the MHSAA's original decision, GRCC said the student whose eligibility was in question enrolled in the school in January 2026. His family moved over the summer, and the school received a letter from the MHSAA confirming his athletic eligibility, according to Grand Rapids Catholic Central.

In mid-October, the MHSAA notified GRCC that it had received new information about the family's residence, reopening an inquiry into whether the student completed a "full and complete move" to satisfy the MHSAA's rules regarding athletic transfers. The school held the player out of its final two regular season games.

On Friday, Oct. 30, a Grand Rapids Catholic Central student, Noah Zainea, filed for a temporary restraining order against the MHSAA's decision, which was granted by a Kent County court. The court ordered the MHSAA to reinstate Grand Rapids Catholic Central and schedule its district semifinal game against Comstock Park by the end of Tuesday.

The MHSAA appealed the decision. But the Court of Appeals denied the appeal on Tuesday and sent the decision back to the circuit court, which had its show-cause hearing on Friday morning.

In the meantime, Grand Rapids Catholic Central played Comstock Park on Tuesday, winning the game 56-13. Since the game was played, Comstock Park is not eligible to advance despite the court's ruling to play the game. As a result, Berrien Springs is the only district final winner who did not have to play a game.

According to the MHSAA's Court of Appeals filing, the organization received new information that the athlete in question "had not, in fact, made a complete, bona fide move out of their residence in the Comstock Park school district and the Ineligible Athlete was thus participating in football at GRCC in violation of the Transfer Rule."

articles.title: Michigan High School Football Powerhouse Kicked Out of Playoffs Following Court Ruling
articles.summary: Grand Rapids Catholic Central has been removed from Michigan's Division 5 football playoffs following a court ruling in favor of the MHSAA.
articles.body:
The Grand Rapids Catholic Central football team's roller-coaster postseason has officially come to an end, and this time, there won't be another playoff game.

According to Patrick Nothaft of MLive , Kent County Circuit Court Judge Paul Denenfeld ruled Monday afternoon in favor of the Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA), upholding its decision to remove Catholic Central from the Division 5 football playoffs for using an ineligible player.

The ruling ends a 12-day legal battle that saw the Cougars initially disqualified, temporarily reinstated and eventually removed from the postseason once again.

And for a team hoping to compete for a state championship, it's a heartbreaking conclusion.

Grand Rapids Catholic Central Removed From MHSAA Playoffs

The controversy began October 29 when the MHSAA removed Catholic Central from the playoffs after determining that the Cougars had used an ineligible player in six regular-season games.

The decision forced Catholic Central to forfeit games and eliminated the program from postseason contention. However, the Cougars received a temporary lifeline when Judge Denenfeld issued a restraining order allowing the team to return to the playoffs.

Catholic Central took advantage of that opportunity, defeating Comstock Park 56-13 in its delayed district semifinal on November 3. But Monday's ruling means that victory will not lead to another postseason appearance.

Following the decision, MHSAA Director of Communications Geoff Kimmerly released a statement through the association.

"The MHSAA is thankful for the Court's prompt decision today, confirming the integrity of the MHSAA's eligibility rules, which all of our member schools expect to be enforced as written," Kimmerly said.

Court Ruling Changes Division 5 Playoff Bracket

As a result of Monday's ruling, Catholic Central will not play its scheduled district final against Berrien Springs on Tuesday. Instead, Berrien Springs (10-1) will receive a forfeit victory and advance to Saturday's regional championship game.

The Shamrocks will face Grand Rapids West Catholic (9-2) at 1 p.m. Saturday on West Catholic's home field. The winner will move one step closer to reaching the Division 5 state championship game.

For Catholic Central, the decision marks a stunning end to a season that appeared to have been saved by the courts just days earlier. The Cougars won their opportunity to return to the field, only to have their championship hopes taken away again.

The MHSAA has maintained that its eligibility rules must be enforced consistently, and Monday's ruling supports its authority to do so in this case. But for the Catholic Central players who had nothing to do with the eligibility violation, it's a difficult way to see their season end.

Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs needs surgery on his broken finger and will miss up to three weeks, according to reporting from Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports on Monday .

Matt LaFleur will speak with the media on Monday afternoon. Packers Wire will update this post if LaFleur confirms the need for surgery.

Jacobs suffered the injury in the first quarter of Sunday's win over the New England Patriots. He left the game and did not return because he was having problems gripping the football.

Missing up to three games suggests Jacobs will not need to go on injured reserve, which would require missing a minimum of four games.

The Packers face the Minnesota Vikings , Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints over the next four weeks. Green Bay has a bye in Week 11. If Jacobs returned after missing three games, he'd be back for Week 14 against the Buffalo Bills.

The big question now: Will the Packers use the trade deadline to add help at running back? Jacobs won't miss the rest of the season, but the run game could use the spark. MarShawn Lloyd is also dealing with a knee injury. The only healthy running backs on the roster are Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. entering Week 10.

articles.title: Chargers players address nightmare of season after loss to Texans
articles.summary: A handful of Chargers players got candid after the team’s eighth consecutive loss to start the season.
articles.body:
The Chargers aren't going anywhere this season. After eight games, the Bolts still haven't collected a win, continuing their nightmare season.

Sunday's loss was arguably their worst of the season. Despite scoring two touchdowns in the contest after not scoring one since Week 5 against the Broncos , the Chargers looked as bad as they have looked this season, and that's saying something.

Los Angeles fell to the Texans , 44-22. This season is as good as over for the Chargers; however, that's not the mentality the team is carrying, even though they remain the only winless team.

Safety Tony Jefferson believes the team will find a solution to their dreadful start.

"First and foremost - just stay together. Secondly - watch the tape and fix the leaks, Jefferson said .

"The proof is in the pudding in the tape, so we'll watch that, fix it and then we'll get back to it."

Running back Keaton Mitchell echoed the same sentiment.

"We have to keep going, keep our head up, continue to work every week and hopefully we'll get one," Mitchell said .

The Chargers' offense mustered two touchdowns, both in garbage time in the fourth quarter. Quentin Johnston's touchdown catch ended the team's 37 straight drives without a touchdown.

Tight end Charlie Kolar couldn't believe the streak.

"37," Kolar said in surprise after he was told about the streak . "I wish you hadn't told me that.

"It is so hard mentally and emotionally to be present. I didn't even know we hadn't scored in that long."

"It's been one of the most frustrating years of my career… you gotta just do everything in your power to stay as locked in where your feet are, and just get better," Kolar said.

Offensive tackle Joe Alt said he's going to look internally to try and fix the issues.

"I'm going to start with myself and look at what I have to get better at," Alt said.

"We all have to get better. The scoreboard doesn't reflect how we wanna play."

The Chargers' offensive line allowed eight sacks on Herbert. LA's 22 points were their most since Week 4 against the Seahawks.

The offense is averaging 15.1 points per game. That's dead last in the league.
